entries.name: 2-XL
entries.def: Talking educational toy robot sold by Mego from 1978 to 1981 and by Tiger Electronics from 1992 to 1995, regarded as the first smart toy.
facts: Considered the first smart toy
Featured among the top ten toys of all time on Playthings' 75th anniversary cover
Name is a pun on "to excel"

entries.name: 360 Eye
entries.def: Dyson's tank tracked vacuum with a panoramic camera crown.

entries.name: 4NE-1
entries.def: Europe's leading commercial humanoid effort, built on Neura's cognitive robot stack.

entries.name: 5DX
entries.def: Automated inspection robot, made by Hewlett Packard and later Agilent Technologies, that took 3D radiographic images of assembled circuit boards to check the solder.
facts: Production passed to Agilent when Hewlett Packard split in 1999
Showed solder thickness in 8 bit grayscale using laminography
Gave process feedback to surface mount assembly lines and caught defects

entries.name: 8A4 class ROUV
entries.def: Remotely operated underwater vehicle of the work class type, developed by China's Shenyang Institute of Automation for jobs ranging from oil platform servicing to salvage and rescue.
facts: Improved from the American AMETEK 2006 design
Preceded by the RECON-IV and followed by the improved 7B8

entries.name: ABISMO
entries.maker: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology
entries.def: Japanese deep sea remotely operated vehicle built by the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology as the replacement for Kaikō, which was lost in 2003.
facts: No other surviving ROV is rated to depths of 11,000 m

entries.name: ACM III
entries.def: Snake robot built by Shigeo Hirose, among the first machines to crawl by undulating its body like a real snake.
facts: ACM stands for Active Cord Mechanism

entries.name: Actroid
entries.def: Highly lifelike android created at Osaka University and produced by Kokoro, usually given the appearance of a young Japanese woman.
facts: Debuted at Tokyo's International Robot Exhibition in 2003
Several versions have been produced since its debut

entries.name: ADAM
entries.def: Two armed beverage robot that mixes and serves drinks in arenas, hotels and hospitals, leased to venues as a staffed kiosk replacement.
specs: Two collaborative robot arms on a fixed torso
Cameras for cup and ingredient detection with an animated display face
Recipe driven task sequencing with vision guided grasping on NVIDIA Jetson compute
facts: Served drinks at the 2024 Major League Baseball All-Star Game
Operates as a robot barista at a Kaiser Permanente hospital cafe in California
Deployed at NHL arena concession stands under a leasing model

entries.name: Adelbrecht
entries.def: Ball shaped robot that could talk and interact with people, designed by Martin Spanjaard.

entries.name: Aeo
entries.def: A wheeled care humanoid patrolling Japanese eldercare homes with UV lamps and soft grippers.

entries.name: AEON
entries.def: An industrial humanoid from the metrology giant, aimed at scanning and inspection work.

entries.name: Aerones
entries.def: Rope suspended robotic system that climbs wind turbine blades to clean, inspect, test lightning conductors and repair leading edges.

entries.name: AESOP
entries.def: Robotic arm that held and moved the endoscope camera during keyhole surgery, the first surgical robot cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration.

entries.name: Affetto
entries.def: Research robot developed at the University of Osaka in Japan, first built in 2012.

entries.name: AgBot 2.055W4
entries.def: Wheeled diesel electric autonomous tractor with a three point hitch and power take off that works pre planned field routes without a driver.
specs: Four wheel drive autonomous tractor with three point hitch and power take off
Diesel electric drivetrain rated at 55 kilowatts
Lidar, cameras and corrected satellite positioning
Runs pre planned field routes generated in AgXeed planning software, with remote monitoring
facts: Launched as AgXeed's wheeled model at the Cereals event in the United Kingdom
Demonstrated very low ground pressure during autonomous celeriac planting in the Netherlands
Sold alongside tracked AgBot models through European farm machinery dealers

entries.name: AgiBot A2
entries.def: Interactive service humanoid from a Shanghai company, holder of the Guinness record for the longest continuous walk by a humanoid robot.
specs: In house electric joint modules in a full size bipedal leg design
Onboard rechargeable battery with hot swap support
Depth cameras, lidar and microphone array for interaction
AgiBot vision language action models trained on large in house teleoperation datasets
facts: Guinness World Record for the longest journey walked by a humanoid robot, 106.286 kilometres in November 2025
Completed a 24 hour autonomous walk in temperatures approaching 40 degrees Celsius
Sold alongside wheeled A2-W and lower cost variants of the same generation

entries.name: Agile ONE
entries.def: Humanoid robot introduced in 2025 by Agile Robots, a robotics company from Germany.

entries.name: AI Suitcase
entries.def: Navigation robot in the form of a suitcase that guides people with visual impairments, developed in 2021 as part of a museum artificial intelligence project.

entries.name: Ai-Da
entries.def: Humanoid robot artist, completed in 2019 by Engineered Arts, that produces drawings, paintings and sculptures.
facts: Named after Ada Lovelace
Draws people in pencil using a bionic hand and cameras in its eyes

entries.name: aibo ERS-1000
entries.def: Sony's revival of its robot dog, a twenty two axis home companion with camera based recognition and cloud connected behaviour.
specs: Rechargeable lithium ion battery with charging station
Front and rear cameras, time of flight sensor, four microphones, touch sensors
Onboard and cloud behaviour learning with mapping and face recognition
facts: Twenty two axes of movement, more than any earlier AIBO
Sold in Japan from January 2018 and withdrawn from sale in 2026 with owner support continuing

entries.name: AIBO ERS-110
entries.def: Sony's first consumer robot dog, an eighteen joint autonomous quadruped sold as an entertainment pet rather than a research machine.
specs: Colour camera, stereo microphones, touch and acceleration sensors
facts: First three thousand units sold in about twenty minutes in Japan in June 1999
Opened the consumer entertainment robot market at about 250,000 yen per unit

entries.name: AIBO ERS-7
entries.def: Consumer entertainment robot in Sony's AIBO series, released in 2003 as the first model the company explicitly presented as a dog.
facts: First released in 2003
Sony's final robot before its robotics division was dissolved in 2006
Succeeded in 2018 by the ERS-1000

entries.name: Aiko Chihira
entries.def: Humanoid android from Toshiba that greeted shoppers as a receptionist at a Mitsukoshi department store in Tokyo.

entries.name: Air-Cobot
entries.def: Wheeled collaborative robot from a French research project, built to check aircraft during maintenance while working alongside human staff.
facts: Research covered autonomous navigation, collaboration with humans and nondestructive testing
Partners included research laboratories and industrial companies

entries.name: AISoy1
entries.def: Consumer pet robot from Spain's AISoy Robotics, counted among the first with emotional learning, whose decisions weigh logical and emotional factors rather than fixed replies.
facts: Can hold dialogues with people and interact with other robots

entries.name: Ajeeb
entries.def: Fake chess automaton built by cabinet maker Charles Hooper, which appeared to play on its own while a skilled human player hidden inside made the moves.
facts: The Royal Polytechnical Institute hosted its first showing in 1868
Its matches attracted tens of thousands of onlookers
Played against Harry Houdini, Theodore Roosevelt and O. Henry

entries.name: Albert HUBO
entries.def: Walking humanoid robot that mounts a head on a full size two legged frame, based on the HUBO biped from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology.
facts: The HUBO platform was released on 6 January 2005
Stands 1.37 m tall and weighs 57 kg
Creator Jun-Ho Oh says the name Hubo is not an abbreviation

entries.name: Alex
entries.def: An upper body humanoid from IHMC lineage, aimed at manipulation research and industry.

entries.name: Alice
entries.def: Tiny cube shaped mobile robot measuring 2 by 2 by 2 cm, created at the Autonomous Systems Lab of the École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne.
facts: Work on it ran from 1998 to 2004 in Lausanne, Switzerland
Has belonged to the Institute of Robotics and Intelligent Systems in Zürich since 2006

entries.name: Aliengo
entries.def: The research quadruped that carried Unitree into universities worldwide.

entries.name: Allen
entries.def: Wheeled research robot that Rodney Brooks's group built in the late 1980s, the first they based on the subsumption architecture.
facts: Carried sonar range sensing and odometry
Relied on a separate Lisp machine off board to run its control system
Looked like a footstool on wheels

entries.name: Alpha Mini
entries.def: A palm sized educational humanoid teaching coding in classrooms.

entries.name: AlphaDog
entries.def: Chinese quadruped platform marketed for education, security and delivery work, launched with claims of unusually high running speed.
specs: Electric joint actuators, three per leg
facts: Stated top speed of about 15 km/h at its 2021 launch
Sold as a family of quadrupeds spanning education units and larger patrol platforms

entries.name: ALPHRED 2
entries.def: Radially symmetric four limbed robot from UCLA that walks in any direction, uses two limbs as arms and can roll on its feet.
specs: Custom back drivable BEAR electric actuators, three per limb
Onboard torque control with several locomotion modes
facts: Radially symmetric layout lets it walk in any direction without turning
Can convert two of its four limbs into arms for manipulation

refs.label: UCLA Robotics and Mechanisms Laboratory website

entries.name: Alter 3
entries.def: An android artist with a neural network nervous system; conducted an opera.

entries.name: Amazon Scout
entries.def: Six wheeled cooler sized sidewalk delivery robot that Amazon field tested in four United States neighbourhoods before ending the programme in 2022.
specs: Six wheeled electric drive with a hinged lid cargo compartment
Autonomous sidewalk route following, accompanied by a human attendant during public trials
facts: First field test launched in Snohomish County, Washington, in January 2019
Later tests ran in Irvine, California, Atlanta, Georgia, and Franklin, Tennessee
Amazon ended Scout field tests in October 2022, the same month FedEx cancelled its Roxo robot

entries.name: Ameca
entries.def: The grey faced expressive android whose stunned expressions became the face of the AI era.

entries.name: Amiga
entries.def: Modular open source electric farm robot with adjustable track width, used by small farms and researchers to carry tools, sensors and custom implements.
specs: Four independently driven electric wheels on a reconfigurable frame with adjustable track width
Depth cameras and satellite positioning, with expansion ports for user sensors
Open source stack supporting teleoperation, taught routes and row following, extensible by the user
facts: Hardware and software are published openly and used as a teaching and research platform
Founded by robotics engineer Ethan Rublee, previously a computer vision engineer in industry
Marketed to small and mid sized specialty crop farms rather than broadacre operations

entries.name: AMOR
entries.def: Autonomous robot built for outdoor operation at the University of Siegen in Germany, working without direct human control.

entries.name: Andromeda
entries.def: Surgical robot developed to carry out parts of procedures autonomously rather than only extending a surgeon's hands.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Andromeda Surgical

entries.name: Andy Warhol Robot
entries.def: Animatronic figure of Andy Warhol that the artist created in 1981 to serve as a self portrait.

entries.name: ANYmal
entries.def: The industrial inspection quadruped patrolling offshore platforms and plants, offered in explosion proof form.

entries.name: ANYmal B
entries.def: First ANYmal generation, a sealed electric quadruped with torque controlled joints sold to research groups and early industrial pilots.
specs: Twelve ANYdrive series elastic electric actuators
Rotating lidar, depth cameras, joint torque sensors, inertial measurement unit
Onboard state estimation, terrain mapping and navigation
facts: Used in the 2019 Science Robotics work that transferred learned locomotion policies from simulation to hardware
First generation of the ANYmal line, derived from ETH Zurich's StarlETH

entries.name: ANYmal C
entries.def: Industrial version of ANYmal, packaged for autonomous inspection rounds in power plants, chemical works and offshore facilities.
specs: Twelve ANYdrive series elastic electric actuators
Swappable lithium ion battery with autonomous docking
Rotating lidar, depth cameras, zoom and thermal cameras, ultrasonic microphone
Autonomous mission execution with docking and remote supervision
facts: Legged element of team CERBERUS, winner of the DARPA Subterranean Challenge final in 2021
Deployed for routine unmanned inspection rounds in industrial plants and offshore installations

entries.name: ANYmal D
entries.def: Current ANYbotics inspection quadruped, a fifty kilogram sealed machine that walks industrial plants on its own and returns to dock.
specs: Twelve ANYdrive series elastic electric actuators
Swappable lithium ion battery with autonomous docking
Sixteen channel lidar, depth cameras, 4K zoom camera, thermal camera, ultrasonic microphone
Autonomous mission execution with mapping, docking and remote supervision
facts: Rated IP67 and used for unmanned inspection on industrial sites including offshore platforms
Climbs standard industrial stairs, which lets it inspect multi level process plants

entries.name: ANYmal X
entries.def: The explosion proof ANYmal certified for oil, gas and chemical plants.

entries.name: Aoi Erika
entries.def: Android announcer created for the television network Nippon TV, introduced in 2017 and standing 166 cm tall.

entries.name: Apollo
entries.def: A warehouse humanoid designed around swappable batteries and friendly form language; piloted with Mercedes-Benz and GXO.

entries.name: Aquanaut
entries.def: Underwater robot that cruises as an autonomous vehicle and then opens into a two armed remotely operated vehicle at its work site.

entries.name: Arachno-Bot
entries.maker: Fraunhofer Institute of Manufacturing Engineering and Automation
entries.def: Eight legged spider inspired robot developed in 2011 at the Fraunhofer Institute of Manufacturing Engineering and Automation in Stuttgart to survey areas too dangerous for people.
facts: Each leg uses an electrohydraulic soft joint modeled on a spider's
Mostly plastic, produced by 3D printing with selective laser sintering
Able to crawl, climb and jump

entries.name: Archie
entries.def: Teen sized humanoid robot over 120 cm tall, developed from 2004 by TU Wien in Austria and the University of Manitoba in Canada.
facts: Work began in 2004 under Professor Peter Kopacek
Balance is handled by a central controller called the Spinal system
Lower body brushless motors provide 50 Nm at the gearbox output

entries.name: Argo
entries.def: Uncrewed camera sled towed deep underwater, developed by Robert Ballard at Woods Hole's Deep Submergence Laboratory, that helped find the wreck of the Titanic in 1985.
facts: Also helped locate the wreck of the Bismarck in 1989

entries.name: Argus
entries.def: Robotic camera platform from MIT's City Scanning project that captured omnidirectional images tagged with their geographic position, dating from 1990.

entries.name: ARI
entries.def: A wheeled social humanoid built for reception desks and human robot interaction studies.

entries.name: ARMAR-6
entries.def: A collaborative wheeled humanoid that hands tools to technicians and learns from demonstration.

entries.name: ARMAR-III
entries.def: Kitchen oriented humanoid from Karlsruhe with 43 degrees of freedom on a holonomic wheeled base, used for household manipulation research.
specs: Electric motors with harmonic drive gears and tendon driven hands
Stereo foveated camera head, microphones, force and torque sensing in the arms
Task level planning with learning from human demonstration
facts: Central platform of the German collaborative research centre on humanoid robots
Worked for years in a full sized mock kitchen

entries.name: Armatron
entries.def: Joystick controlled toy robot arm from Tomy, sold through Radio Shack stores in the United States from 1984, with no automatic functions.
facts: Six degrees of freedom, including a gripper with two fingers
Wrist and shoulder could rotate without limit
Looked like a 1980s industrial robot but was fully manual

entries.name: ARTOS
entries.def: Autonomous robot for transport and service tasks, developed at the University of Kaiserslautern in Germany.

entries.name: Ascento Guard
entries.def: A two wheeled jumping security robot balancing on legs with wheels for feet.

entries.name: Aseon Pod
entries.def: Robotic micro depot that charges, cleans and services self driving cars between trips.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Aseon Labs

entries.name: ASIMO
entries.def: The world's most famous walking robot for two decades; retired to museum duty in 2022.

entries.name: ASRA C1
entries.def: Sony's dual armed cooking research robot developed with Carnegie Mellon.

entries.name: Astro
entries.def: A household monitor upon wheels; a camera, a screen and a disposition, sold as a home robot.

entries.name: AstroAnt
entries.def: Matchbox sized magnetic wheeled robot designed to crawl over a lunar rover's surface and take thermal readings while it drives.
specs: Four magnetic wheels for driving on metal surfaces
Thermal sensor and inertial measurement unit
Short range wireless control from its host rover
facts: Designed to inspect a rover while riding on it
Flew on IM-2 in 2025 without being deployed

entries.name: Astrobee
entries.def: System of three cube shaped free flying robots from NASA's Ames Research Center that helps astronauts with routine chores aboard the International Space Station.
facts: The three robots are named Honey, Queen and Bumble
Each robot is a cube 31.75 cm on a side
A docking station lets the robots recharge

entries.name: Asuro
entries.def: Programmable robot able to act autonomously, carrying out behaviours that its user writes and loads as software.

entries.name: Atalante
entries.def: Self balancing exoskeleton from Wandercraft that lets people with paralysis walk without crutches.

entries.name: ATHLETE
entries.def: A six limbed wheel legged lunar cargo hauler that rolls or walks as terrain demands.

entries.name: Atlas (electric)
entries.def: The all electric successor to the hydraulic Atlas; unveiled for enterprise material handling at CES 2026.

entries.name: Atlas (hydraulic)
entries.def: The hydraulic research humanoid whose parkour and backflips defined a decade of legged robotics.

entries.name: Atom
entries.def: A desktop arm maker's leap to full humanoids, priced to undercut the field.

entries.name: ATRIAS
entries.maker: Oregon State University, Dynamic Robotics Laboratory
entries.def: Spring mass biped from Oregon State built to test whether a legged robot could match the dynamics and efficiency of running birds.
specs: Series elastic actuators with fiberglass leg springs
Joint encoders and an inertial measurement unit
facts: Physical test of the spring loaded inverted pendulum model of running
Demonstrated at the 2015 DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals

refs.label: Oregon State University, Dynamic Robotics Laboratory website

entries.name: ATRIS
entries.def: Four wheeled outdoor patrol robot used for security rounds at Chinese industrial parks and substations, carrying cameras, thermal imaging and lidar.
specs: Four wheeled electric drive chassis with a raised sensor mast
Lidar, panoramic cameras and thermal imaging
Autonomous patrol along mapped routes with remote operator handoff
facts: Used for outdoor security patrols at Chinese industrial parks and electrical substations
A pandemic variant carried thermal screening and public address equipment
Built by UBTECH Robotics of Shenzhen, which also produces humanoid and education robots

entries.name: Audi Lunar Quattro
entries.maker: Planetary Transportation Systems and Audi AG
entries.def: Small German lunar rover developed in 2015 by engineers of the PTScientists team, with backing from Audi and partners in several countries.
facts: Mass of 35 kg

entries.name: Automower 450X
entries.def: The descendant of the world's first robotic lawn mower, three decades on the job.

entries.name: Autonomous Benthic Explorer
entries.def: Autonomous underwater vehicle operated by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution that surveyed broad stretches of seabed down to 4500 m until its loss at sea in 2010.
facts: Completed 222 missions between 1996 and 2010
Depth rating of 4500 m (14,674 ft)
Scouted targets for more capable crewed vehicles and ROVs

entries.name: Autonomous Shipboard Humanoid
entries.def: Humanoid robot developed at the United States Naval Research Laboratory with Virginia Tech and the University of Pennsylvania to move around ships, climb ladders and fight fires.
facts: Meant to respond to emergencies and follow visual commands from people
Already able to walk, among other abilities

entries.name: AutoPallet
entries.def: Swarm of small mobile robots that move cardboard boxes and install into existing warehouses.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, AutoPallet Robotics

entries.name: AUV ABYSS
entries.def: REMUS 6000 autonomous underwater vehicle built by Hydroid in 2008 and owned by GEOMAR, used to map the deep seabed and gather data from the water column.
facts: Named after the abyssal plain, the seafloor zone between 2000 and 6000 m
Runs on lithium ion batteries for dives of up to 22 hours
About 4 m long

entries.name: AUV-150
entries.def: Indian autonomous underwater vehicle under development by scientists at the Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute in Durgapur, West Bengal, with support from IIT Kharagpur.
facts: Sponsored by India's Ministry of Earth Sciences

entries.name: Ava 500
entries.def: Autonomous office telepresence robot from iRobot that drove itself to a chosen meeting room, using video equipment from Cisco.

entries.name: Avadin
entries.def: Care robot for older people developed by the South Korean company Wonderful Platform, also known by the name Dasom.

entries.name: Avride
entries.def: The delivery rover formerly of Yandex, ferrying food across campuses with Grubhub.

entries.name: Avride delivery robot
entries.def: Six wheeled sidewalk delivery robot that carries Uber Eats orders in several United States cities, navigating autonomously with remote operators available to assist.
specs: Six wheeled electric drive with a lockable insulated cargo bin
Autonomous sidewalk navigation with remote operator assistance
facts: Launched sidewalk delivery with Uber Eats in Jersey City in February 2025, then Arlington, Virginia, and Miami in 2026
Spun out of the Yandex self driving unit and reorganised as Avride under Nebius
Raised 375 million dollars from Uber and Nebius to scale its autonomy fleet

entries.name: Axle Robot Kit
entries.def: Robot kit from the American company True Robotics that students in grades 6 to 8 build for classroom learning.

entries.name: Azalea
entries.def: Robots that load and sort checked luggage in airport baggage halls.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Azalea Robotics Corporation

entries.name: B2-W
entries.def: A wheeled variant of the B2 that skates stairs and slopes on powered hubs.

entries.name: Ballie
entries.def: A rolling home companion ball with a built in projector, launched after six years of teasers.

entries.name: Banryu
entries.def: Robot product model developed in Japan and manufactured by the electronics company Sanyo.

entries.name: Baxter
entries.def: Two armed collaborative industrial robot from Rethink Robotics, the startup founded by Rodney Brooks, that has an animated face.
facts: The first unit was completed on 22 September 2011

entries.name: BB-8 by Sphero
entries.def: App controlled rolling toy modelled on the droid from the 2015 Star Wars film, a ball with a magnetically held head.

entries.name: Beam
entries.def: The telepresence pioneer that let Edward Snowden wander conference stages.

entries.name: Bear Flag autonomous tractor
entries.def: Retrofit kit that turned existing farm tractors and implements into driverless machines; the company was acquired by Deere.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Bear Flag Robotics

entries.name: Bee-Bot
entries.def: Educational robot intended for use in teaching, giving learners a physical machine to experiment with during lessons.

entries.name: BellaBot
entries.def: Four tray delivery robot with a cat like animated face, used in restaurants and hotels to carry dishes to tables and clear them away.
specs: Rechargeable battery with a charging dock
Lidar, three depth cameras and tray load sensors
Laser or visual SLAM with automatic route planning and obstacle avoidance
facts: Carries up to 10 kg on each of four trays
Pudu Robotics was founded in Shenzhen in 2016
Offers laser positioning with no ceiling height restriction

entries.name: Benthic Rover II
entries.def: Autonomous tracked seafloor rover that has monitored carbon cycling on the abyssal plain off California for years at a time.
specs: Pair of wide rubber tracks for short repositioning moves
Battery pack drawing about two watts on average
Respirometer chambers, oxygen sensors, fluorescence and still cameras, temperature loggers
Fully autonomous year long measurement cycles with no tether
facts: Works unattended on the abyssal seafloor for about a year per deployment
Recorded large pulses of sinking food reaching the seafloor between 2015 and 2020

refs.label: Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute website

entries.name: Berkeley Lower Extremity Exoskeleton
entries.maker: Berkeley Robotics and Human Engineering Laboratory
entries.def: Lower body powered exoskeleton developed by the Berkeley Robotics and Human Engineering Laboratory at the University of California, Berkeley, with DARPA funding, to add strength to leg movements.
facts: DARPA supplied $50 million in initial funding in 2001
A prototype was shown at the DARPA Technical Symposium in 2004

entries.name: Bex
entries.def: A rideable robot ibex that carries a person on its back and kneels on wheels.

entries.name: BHR-2
entries.def: Second generation Beijing Institute of Technology humanoid that performed tai chi and broadsword forms to demonstrate whole body balance control.
specs: Gait pattern generation with online balance compensation
facts: Performed tai chi routines and broadsword forms
Part of the BHR humanoid series that began in 2002

entries.name: Big Mouth Billy Bass
entries.def: Singing animatronic novelty in the form of a largemouth bass, created by Gemmy Industries and widely popular from the late 1990s into the early 2000s.
facts: Gemmy Industries came up with the design in 1998

entries.name: BigDog
entries.def: The gasoline engined pack mule whose recovery from a kick announced the legged robot age.

entries.name: BINA48
entries.def: Humanoid robot head with chatbot software for basic conversation, built by Hanson Robotics in 2010 and made to look like Bina Aspen.
facts: Belongs to Martine Rothblatt's Terasem Movement
Bina Aspen, its model, is Rothblatt's wife
Name stands for Breakthrough Intelligence via Neural Architecture 48

entries.name: Bio-Intelligent Cyborg Insect
aka: BCI,bio-intelligent cyborg insect,biointelligent cyborg insect,UV-controlled cyborg insect
entries.def: Biohybrid robotic system that steers living insects without surgery by using ultraviolet light, relying on their natural tendency to move away from it.

entries.name: BionicKangaroo
entries.def: Kangaroo shaped jumping robot from Festo that, like the animal, recovers energy from each hop and puts it into the next.
facts: Design drew on Festo's study of how kangaroos move

entries.name: BISAM
entries.def: Mammal like four legged walking machine from Karlsruhe, built to study adaptive gait control with an articulated trunk.
specs: Layered reflex and gait selection controller
facts: Used an actuated spine as well as four legs, unusual for the period
Part of the wave of biologically inspired walking machines built in Germany in the 1990s

entries.name: Bistrobot
entries.def: Automated sandwich line from a San Francisco startup that assembled orders while customers watched.

entries.name: Bittle
entries.def: Palm sized programmable robot dog kit with nine powered joints, sold as an education platform for coding and robotics classes.
specs: Six axis inertial measurement unit, infrared receiver, optional camera and touch sensors
OpenCat gait framework on an Arduino compatible board
facts: Raised over 500,000 US dollars on Kickstarter in 2020
Runs the open source OpenCat framework, one of the most used open quadruped code bases

entries.name: Bluefin-21
entries.def: Autonomous underwater vehicle from Bluefin Robotics for defence, commercial and scientific tasks, best known for its part in the 2014 hunt for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370.
facts: Searched for the wreckage of Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 in April 2014

entries.name: BlueROV2
entries.def: Modular underwater remotely operated vehicle from the American company Blue Robotics, offered at low cost and run on open source control software.
facts: Released in 2016
Used in underwater research, inspection and education

entries.name: Boaty McBoatface
entries.def: British autonomous underwater vehicle belonging to the Autosub Long Range class, run by the National Oceanography Centre for scientific research.
facts: One of six vehicles in its class
The class was launched in 2017
Can be launched from the shore

entries.name: Boe-Bot
entries.def: Wheeled educational robot kit sold by Parallax, built around a BASIC Stamp microcontroller board with two servo driven wheels on an aluminum chassis.
facts: Its name abbreviates Board of Education robot
Produced and marketed by Parallax Inc from 1998 onward
Common in robotics courses from junior high through college

entries.name: Boost
entries.def: Autonomous mobile manipulator that inspects and services equipment in data centers.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Boost Robotics

entries.name: Booster T1
entries.def: Mid size developer humanoid sold to universities and robot sports teams, widely used in RoboCup humanoid league competition.
specs: Electric joint modules with four degree of freedom arms and no standard end effectors
Onboard battery giving about two hours walking or four standing
RGB-D camera, microphone array, speaker, nine axis IMU
Open software development kit with a simulation environment
facts: Widely adopted by RoboCup humanoid league competition teams
Combines an Intel Core i7 with an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin for onboard learning
Sold internationally through robotics distributors as a developer platform

entries.name: Bossa Nova 2020
entries.def: Walmart's shelf scanner fleet, cancelled overnight when the retailer changed course.

entries.name: Bossa Nova shelf scanning robot
entries.def: Tall camera tower on a wheeled base that scanned supermarket shelves for gaps and pricing errors, best known from a large Walmart rollout.
specs: Wheeled base with a tall camera mast
Vertical array of cameras with depth sensing
Map based aisle navigation among shoppers with off robot image analysis
facts: Deployed in hundreds of Walmart stores, with reports of plans for about 1,000
Walmart ended the contract in November 2020 and the retail robot business wound down

refs.label: Wikipedia search, Bossa Nova shelf scanning robot

entries.name: BotBuilt
entries.def: Robotic cells that assemble wall panels and roof trusses for house framing.

entries.name: Botvac D7
entries.def: The laser mapping vacuum pioneer whose maker closed in 2023.

entries.name: Braava
entries.def: Roomba's quiet mopping sibling for hard floors.

entries.name: Bridget
entries.def: Airbus Mars rover testbed used in the Stevenage Mars Yard and in Atacama Desert trials of European rover autonomy software.
specs: Six wheels in three bogies with steering
Battery electric with cabled supply during yard tests
Stereo navigation cameras with mast mounted instruments
Testbed for European autonomous navigation software
facts: Operated in the Atacama Desert during ESA's SAFER Mars analogue trial
Long running testbed for European rover autonomy

entries.name: BRUIE
aka: Buoyant Rover for Under Ice Exploration
entries.def: Buoyant two wheeled rover that drives upside down along the underside of ice, tested in Antarctic and Alaskan lakes.
specs: Two studded wheels that drive along the underside of ice
Battery with very low draw while parked against the ice
Cameras with lights, dissolved oxygen, salinity, pressure and temperature sensors
Teleoperated on a thin tether with long duration station keeping
facts: Drives along the underside of ice rather than the seabed
Tested under Antarctic sea ice at Casey Station in 2019

entries.name: Buddharoid
entries.def: Japanese robot monk created by Kyoto University researchers with technology company partners to give Buddhist spiritual guidance, unveiled at a temple in Kyoto.
facts: First presented at Shoren in Temple, Kyoto

entries.name: Buddy

entries.def: Female humanoid toy robot from WowWee that responds to what it sees, hears and feels, and accepts programmed sequences of movements.
facts: Unveiled at CES in January 2008
Planned at $99 and selling for $89.99 by 2009

entries.name: FIDO
aka: Field Integrated Design and Operations rover
entries.def: Terrestrial prototype rover used to rehearse Mars Exploration Rover science operations in desert field tests before the 2003 launches.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive with four corner steering
Mast mounted panoramic and infrared imagers, microscopic imager, mini corer
Remote operations with autonomous navigation and instrument placement
facts: Trained the science teams that later operated Spirit and Opportunity
Carried a mini corer to practise rock sampling in the field

entries.name: Figure 01
entries.def: Figure's first full scale humanoid; proved the platform before its successors took over.

entries.name: Figure 02
entries.def: The second generation Figure humanoid, piloted on BMW production lines with onboard conversational reasoning.

entries.name: Figure 03
entries.def: Figure's third machine, built for the Helix vision language action model and scaled to dozens of units at customer sites.

entries.name: Fingerlings
entries.def: Line of small robotic toy creatures from WowWee that cling to a finger and blink or blow kisses when they sense touch or sound.
facts: Released by WowWee in 2017
Larger plush Fingerlings Hugs versions offer the same interactivity

entries.name: Flakey
entries.def: Research robot developed at SRI International's Artificial Intelligence Center to succeed the earlier Shakey robot.
facts: Appeared on the television series Scientific American Frontiers

entries.name: Flame
entries.def: Humanoid walking robot built by Daan Hobbelen at Delft University of Technology to study how humans walk, standing 130 cm tall and weighing 15 kg.
facts: Came out of Delft University's Mechanical Engineering department

entries.name: FlashBot
entries.def: A hotel delivery robot that calls elevators and phones guests on arrival.

entries.name: Fleetzero
entries.def: Electric cargo vessels designed to run with remote supervision instead of a full crew.

entries.name: FLEX
entries.def: Large commercial lunar rover prototype that can carry cargo or two standing astronauts, demonstrated in field trials in the California desert.
specs: Four wheel drive and steering with a payload lifting frame
Teleoperation with autonomous point to point driving
facts: Full scale prototype driven with an astronaut aboard in Death Valley
Designed to carry up to 1,500 kg of modular payload

entries.name: Flex Robotic System
entries.def: Medical snake robot for single port surgery, developed at the Technion in Israel and dating from 2014.

refs.label: Technion, Israel Institute of Technology website

entries.name: FlexPicker
entries.def: High speed parallel arm robot from ABB that picks small items from conveyors, based on the delta design invented by Reymond Clavel at EPFL.
facts: Original model number IRB 340

entries.name: Flippy
entries.def: Robot arm from Miso Robotics that flips burgers and runs deep fryers in fast food kitchens, first placed at CaliBurger.

entries.name: Flywheel
entries.def: Kit that converts existing excavators for remote operation and gathers the data used to train autonomous digging.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Flywheel AI

entries.name: Forerunner K2
entries.def: Industrial humanoid listed from about 30,000 dollars, with 52 joints and eleven degree of freedom hands, aimed at factory material handling.
specs: Electric joint actuators with near zero static holding power draw
More than 80 onboard sensors, 25 force sensing contact points per finger, six axis wrist force torque sensors
Onboard compute rated at 100 trillion operations per second with millimetre level placement
facts: Completed an eight hour continuous livestreamed work session at WAIC 2025
Listed from about 30,000 dollars for the base configuration
Each hand has eleven degrees of freedom with per finger force sensing

entries.name: Fourier GR-2
entries.def: Full size humanoid from a rehabilitation robotics company, sold as a general purpose platform with tactile hands and swappable batteries.
specs: Seven variants of Fourier Smart Actuator with peak torque above 380 newton metres
Detachable swappable battery giving about two hours per pack
Six array tactile sensors per hand, depth cameras, dual joint encoders
Open development platform supplied for third party embodied intelligence work
facts: Announced in September 2024 with twelve degrees of freedom in each hand
Tactile hand sensors identify object shape and material by contact
Built by a company whose earlier products were rehabilitation exoskeletons

entries.name: Freddy II
entries.maker: Department of Machine Intelligence and Perception
entries.def: Experimental robot built at the Department of Machine Intelligence and Perception and active from 1973 to 1976 as the successor to the original Freddy.
facts: Active from 1973 to 1976
Followed the first Freddy, which ran from 1969 to 1971

entries.name: Freight
entries.def: A ROS native mobile base that carried research and warehouses alike; Zebra acquired its maker.

entries.name: Freight500
entries.def: Flat deck autonomous mobile robot that carries up to 500 kg of goods on pallets or roll cages through warehouse and factory aisles.
specs: Safety laser scanners and 3D depth cameras
Laser SLAM with cloud based fleet management and no floor markers
facts: Zebra Technologies acquired Fetch Robotics in 2021
The smaller Freight100 base is widely used in university labs with ROS
A larger Freight1500 handles pallet sized loads

entries.name: Furby
entries.def: Talking robot toy resembling an owl, made by Hasbro subsidiary Tiger Electronics, that became a sought after holiday gift following its October 1998 launch.
facts: First released in October 1998
Over 40 million sold in its original three years of production
Its speech was translated into 17 languages

entries.name: Furhat
entries.def: Conversational social robot from the Swedish company Furhat Robotics, with a humanlike face projected from behind and software for speech recognition and synthesis.
facts: Used in education, healthcare, recruitment and transport
Employed in social robotics studies at several universities

entries.name: Gabi
entries.def: Humanoid robot monk presented by the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism in 2026 as a way to bring the faith closer to younger Koreans.
facts: Introduced at a precept ceremony at Jogyesa Temple, Seoul, on 6 May 2026

entries.name: Gakutensoku
entries.def: Early Japanese robot made by biologist Makoto Nishimura in Osaka during the late 1920s, regarded as the first robot built in East Asia.

entries.name: Galbot G1
entries.def: A wheeled dual armed humanoid running unmanned retail stores around Beijing.

entries.name: GARMI
entries.def: A wheeled geriatric care humanoid doubling as a telemedicine avatar.

entries.name: Gatik autonomous box truck
entries.def: Retrofitted box truck that drives fixed middle mile freight routes between warehouses and stores, running driverless on some routes in the United States.
specs: Autonomy kit retrofitted to medium duty commercial box trucks
Level 4 autonomy constrained to fixed, pre validated middle mile routes with remote monitoring
facts: Made fully driverless commercial box truck deliveries for Walmart in Bentonville, Arkansas, from 2021
Runs middle mile freight for Sam's Club and hauls for Georgia-Pacific through KBX
Reported hundreds of additional trucks planned for United States roads in 2026

entries.name: GD01
entries.def: Large powered exoskeleton made by the Chinese company Unitree Robotics, standing 2.7 m tall with a mass of 500 kg.

entries.name: Gecko Robotics inspection robots
entries.def: Fleet of magnetic wall climbing and crawling robots that scan boilers, tanks, pipelines and ship hulls for wall thickness and corrosion.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Gecko Robotics

entries.name: Geminoid HI-1
entries.maker: ATR Intelligent Robotics and Communication Laboratories with Osaka University
entries.def: Teleoperated android copy of researcher Hiroshi Ishiguro, built to study how human presence transfers through a remotely controlled likeness.
specs: External air compressor and mains power
Operator side motion capture, cameras and microphones in the remote room
Teleoperated, with automatic idle motions such as breathing and blinking
facts: Physical copy of its own creator
Started the Geminoid series of teleoperated androids

refs.label: ATR Intelligent Robotics and Communication Laboratories with Osaka University website

entries.name: Gen3
entries.def: Ultralight seven axis arm from Kinova used in research labs and on mobile robots.

entries.name: Genghis
entries.def: Six legged walking robot resembling an insect, built by Rodney Brooks at MIT and associated with his reactive subsumption architecture for robot behaviour.

entries.name: Genibo
entries.def: Korean entertainment robot dog styled as a bull terrier, sold as a home pet with voice command control.
specs: Colour camera, touch sensors on head, back and flanks, microphones, tilt sensor
Onboard personality and voice command software
facts: One of very few consumer walking robot pets to reach market after Sony ended AIBO
Sold internationally from 2008 at about 1,500 US dollars

entries.name: George
entries.def: British humanoid robot that Tony Sale assembled in 1949 from scrap metal taken off a crashed RAF Wellington bomber.
facts: Reactivated by Sale in 2010
Now exhibited at The National Museum of Computing, Bletchley Park

entries.name: gita
entries.def: A cargo robot from the Vespa family that follows its owner like a rolling suitcase.

entries.name: Global Explorer ROV
entries.def: Deep water remotely operated vehicle made by Chris Nicholson of Deep Sea Systems International and used on research and survey dives deeper than 2,700 m.
facts: Has made many dives below 9,000 feet (2,700 m)
Used on expeditions for National Geographic and NOAA
Its builder, Deep Sea Systems International, is based in Falmouth, Massachusetts

entries.name: Go2-W
entries.def: The consumer Go2 on wheels, rolling where legs would waste energy.

entries.name: GoFa
entries.def: Collaborative arm from ABB with joint torque sensing, meant to be set up by staff without robot programming experience.
facts: Model number CRB 15000

entries.name: GoMate
entries.def: A variable wheel legged humanoid from Guangzhou's auto giant.

entries.name: GR-1
entries.def: A rehabilitation born humanoid produced in volume before most rivals shipped one.

entries.name: GR-100
entries.def: Greenhouse robot from Four Growers that picks ripe tomatoes and records crop data as it travels the heating rails between rows.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Four Growers

entries.name: GR-3
entries.def: A soft touch companion humanoid marking Fourier's turn toward care robotics.

entries.name: Grace
entries.def: A humanlike care android trialled in eldercare and health settings; built for conversation as much as task work.

entries.name: Grip
entries.def: Picking robot that removes contaminants from organic waste streams, learning from every successful and failed grasp.

entries.name: GROVER
aka: Goddard Remotely Operated Vehicle for Exploration and Research
entries.def: Solar powered autonomous rover, designed by students and developed at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center to collect low cost data on the Greenland ice sheet.
facts: Tested on the Greenland ice sheet at Summit Camp from 3 May to 8 June 2013
Operated in temperatures down to minus 30 °C
Science team led by Goddard glaciologist Lora Koenig

entries.name: GSF AutoVacC 6
entries.def: French prototype industrial cleaning robot of the AutoVacC type, built by Robosoft in 1990.

entries.name: Guardian XO
entries.def: Battery powered full body exoskeleton from Sarcos built to let workers lift heavy loads repeatedly.

entries.name: GuRoo
entries.def: Autonomous humanoid research robot built at the University of Queensland's Mobile Robotics Laboratory to study balance, interaction with people and machine learning.
facts: Takes part in RoboCup, the yearly robot soccer competition
Designed to be as close to human form as possible

entries.name: Hadal ARV
entries.def: Chinese hybrid unmanned underwater vehicle from the Shenyang Institute of Automation that can work either autonomously or under remote control, much like Nereus.
facts: Its ARV label means autonomous remotely controlled vehicle
Successor to the Arctic ARV and predecessor of the Hadal 1 ARV
Developer is part of the Chinese Academy of Sciences
Can operate as an autonomous vehicle or a remotely operated one
Chief designer is Tang Yuan-Gui
Chinese counterpart to the Nereus hybrid underwater vehicle

entries.name: Haile
entries.def: Robotic percussionist from the Georgia Institute of Technology that listens to live music through a microphone and plays its own rhythm on a real drum.
facts: Designed in 2006 by Georgia Tech professor Gil Weinberg with student Scott Driscoll
Billed as the first robot to make acoustic percussion rather than play through speakers
Switches between leading and following roles based on what it hears

entries.name: HaiPick
entries.def: A carton climbing autonomous case handler pioneering the ACR category.

entries.name: HAL
entries.maker: University of Tsukuba and Cyberdyne Inc.
entries.def: Powered exoskeleton suit with a soft body, known in full as the Hybrid Assistive Limb, built by Japan's University of Tsukuba and Cyberdyne to boost its wearers' physical abilities.
facts: HAL 3 supports leg function only
HAL 5 is a full body version covering arms, legs and torso

entries.name: Han
entries.def: Social humanoid robot from the Hong Kong firm Hanson Robotics, built mostly as a head with Frubber skin that senses people and gauges their age, gender and emotional expression.
facts: Switched on for the first time in 2015
Debuted at the Global Sources Electronics Fair in 2015
Head can sit on a clear body that exposes its electronics

entries.name: Handle
entries.def: A wheel legged biped that leapt and lifted boxes; its logistics role passed to Stretch.

entries.name: Hardiman
entries.def: Early powered exoskeleton from General Electric, meant to give its wearer the strength to raise 1500 pounds (680 kg) with little effort.
facts: Built by General Electric between 1965 and 1971
Described as the first attempt at a practical powered exoskeleton
Project led by engineer Ralph Mosher, who had earlier worked on the Handyman

entries.name: Hedgehog
entries.def: Robotic growing system that automates mushroom farms.

entries.name: Hello Robot Stretch
entries.def: Lightweight mobile manipulator with a telescoping arm on a vertical mast, built to help people with everyday tasks at home.

entries.name: Herbert
entries.def: Wheeled robot from Rodney Brooks's group at MIT that roamed offices collecting empty soda cans with its arm.

entries.name: Hermes Robotics
entries.def: Retrofit autonomy for street sweepers, sold as a sweeping service.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Hermes Robotics

entries.name: HERO 1
entries.def: The mail order home robot kit that taught a generation of hobbyists.

entries.name: Hexbug
entries.def: Brand of robotic insect toys from Spin Master that borrows from BEAM robotics, its first models imitating six legged arthropods.
facts: First test marketed in the United States through RadioShack
Name refers to its six sided packaging, not its number of legs

entries.name: Hilare
entries.maker: Laboratory for Analysis and Architecture of Systems
entries.def: French mobile robot built in 1977 by the Laboratory for Analysis and Architecture of Systems, its name an acronym for heuristics integrated into software and automation in an evolving robot.

refs.label: Laboratory for Analysis and Architecture of Systems website

entries.name: hitchBOT
entries.def: Hitchhiking robot from Canada, made by academics at McMaster and Ryerson universities, that crossed three countries on rides from strangers before it was destroyed.
facts: Created in 2013 by David Harris Smith and Frauke Zeller
Completed trips through Canada, Germany and the Netherlands
Found stripped and dismembered in Philadelphia in 2015, ending its US trip

entries.name: HOAP
entries.def: Series of humanoid robots made by Fujitsu Automation in Japan and offered as an open architecture platform.
facts: HOAP stands for Humanoid for Open Architecture Platform

entries.name: HolaBot
entries.def: A dish return runner summoned by waving a hand at its sensors.

entries.name: Honda E series
entries.def: Succession of experimental humanoid robots that Honda built in secret from 1986 to 1993, an early stage on the path to the P series and ASIMO.
facts: Kept from the public until Honda announced the P2 in 1996

entries.name: Honda Miimo
entries.def: Battery powered robotic lawn mower model produced by the Japanese company Honda.

entries.name: Honda P series
entries.def: Line of prototype humanoid robots that Honda built from 1993 to 2000, the stage between its experimental E series and the ASIMO robot.
facts: Honda president Hiroyuki Yoshino tied the program to improving human mobility

entries.name: HOSPI
entries.def: Autonomous hospital delivery robot that moves medicines, specimens and records between departments around the clock in locked trays.
specs: Battery with automatic charging and about 4.5 hours to recharge
Laser and obstacle sensors with card reader access control
Follows stored building map data with obstacle avoidance and wireless reporting
facts: Four units entered service at Changi General Hospital in Singapore in 2015, its first hospital outside Japan
Certified to the ISO 13482 service robot safety standard
Carries up to six lockable medication trays

entries.name: HOUND
entries.def: A sprinting quadruped holding a Guinness 100 metre record for its class.

entries.name: HR6
entries.def: Humanoid robot model produced by Dr Robot, a robotics company based in Canada.

entries.name: HRP-2
entries.def: Japan's national research humanoid, star of a hundred university labs.

entries.name: HRP-2P
entries.def: Humanoid robot model in the HRP series, built by the Japanese company Kawada Technologies.

entries.name: HRP-3
entries.maker: Kawada Technologies and National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology
entries.def: Japanese humanoid robot introduced in 2007 by Kawada Technologies in partnership with the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology.

entries.name: HRP-4
entries.def: Slim humanoid from Japan's national research institute AIST and Kawada, lighter than earlier HRP machines.

entries.name: HRP-4C
entries.def: A singing, catwalk walking gynoid built to human proportions for entertainment research.

refs.label: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology website

entries.name: HRP-5P
entries.def: A heavy labour research humanoid that hangs drywall and handles full size panels.

entries.name: HSR
entries.def: Toyota's Human Support Robot, a one armed home helper standard in RoboCup@Home.

entries.name: HUBO
entries.def: Third generation KAIST biped with five fingered hands and independently moving eyes that walked at 1.25 km/h, danced and gripped objects.
specs: Electric servo motors with harmonic drive gears
Onboard computer running zero moment point walking control
facts: Basis for Albert HUBO and the later DRC-Hubo machines
Copies used in the United States as a shared humanoid research platform

refs.label: KAIST Humanoid Robot Research Center website

entries.name: Hugh
entries.def: Robot librarian built as a prototype at Aberystwyth University to locate books for library users and lead them there, though it never went into use.
facts: Designed by William Sachiti and Ariel Ladegaard
First publicised in February 2016

entries.name: Hugo RAS
entries.def: Modular robotic surgery system from Medtronic with an open surgeon console, first used on a patient in Chile in 2021.

entries.name: Human Universal Load Carrier
entries.maker: Ekso Bionics and Berkeley Robotics and Human Engineering Laboratory
entries.def: Untethered hydraulic exoskeleton developed for soldiers by H. Kazerooni's team at Ekso Bionics, intended to help wearers carry loads of up to 200 pounds.
facts: Developed at the Berkeley Robotics and Human Engineering Laboratory from 2000
Unveiled on 26 February 2009 at the AUSA Winter Symposium, with Lockheed Martin taking an exclusive licence
Judged a failure because it hampered movement and increased muscle strain

entries.name: Husky
entries.def: The default outdoor research base of a thousand robotics papers.

entries.name: Husky A300
entries.def: The modernised Husky, weatherproofed and faster for field research.

entries.name: HyQ
entries.def: Hydraulically actuated quadruped from the Italian Institute of Technology used to study dynamic legged locomotion.
facts: Predecessor of HyQReal

entries.name: HyQReal
entries.def: A hydraulic heavyweight that once towed a three tonne aircraft.

entries.name: I-Bot
entries.def: Small robot from Microbric, given out in kit form by the Adelaide Advertiser newspaper in 2005 to introduce readers to electronics and robotics.
facts: Distributed through the Adelaide Advertiser in South Australia in November and December 2005

entries.name: i-Cybie
entries.def: Robotic toy dog produced in Hong Kong by Silverlit Toys from 2000 to 2006 that reacted to sound, touch, motion and spoken commands.
facts: Manufactured from 2000 to 2006
Could recharge its batteries by itself at a docking station
First toy made in large numbers to feature advanced voice recognition

entries.name: Ibn Sina Robot
entries.def: Android robot made in 2009 by Nikolaos Mavridis and David Hanson in the United Arab Emirates, described as the first android able to converse in Arabic.
facts: Built in 2009 at the Interactive Robots and Media Lab
One of its creators was Hanson Robotics founder David Hanson

entries.name: ibuki
entries.def: A child android on wheels, built to study affinity with young humanoids.

entries.name: IceMole
entries.def: Autonomous, steerable ice probe developed at FH Aachen in Germany that melts and screws its way through ice for polar, glacier and space research.
facts: Steerable while melting through ice, and retrievable once its work is done
Uses a driving ice screw to push through soil layers and debris in the ice

entries.name: iCub
entries.def: A child sized open source humanoid distributed to dozens of labs to study embodied cognition.

entries.name: Idefix
entries.def: Small rover built by France's CNES and Germany's DLR with help from JAXA, carried by the MMX spacecraft to set down on and explore the Martian moon Phobos.
facts: Lifted off aboard MMX on 19 October 2026
Mass 23.47 kg; 41 cm long, 37 cm wide and 23 cm high
Meant to survey Phobos ahead of MMX's own landing and sample collection

entries.name: iDog
entries.def: Robot dog toy from Sega that flashes its lights and dances along to music played into it from an iPod or other MP3 player.
facts: Called eDog in the German, Italian and Dutch markets

entries.name: Indego
entries.def: Lightweight powered hip and knee exoskeleton developed at Vanderbilt University and sold by Parker Hannifin.

entries.name: Indro
entries.def: Indian humanoid robot that stands 6.5 feet (2.0 m) tall, making it the tallest of its kind in the country.
facts: Height of 6.5 feet (2.0 m), a record for humanoid robots in India

entries.name: Inkha
entries.def: Interactive robot head that Mat Walker and Peter S. Longyear built at King's College London in 2002.
facts: Created in 2002 at King's College London

entries.name: InLoop
entries.def: Robot arms that pick and pack online orders, with remote operators stepping in when a grasp fails.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, InLoop Robotics

entries.name: InMoov
entries.def: Humanoid robot assembled from plastic body parts made on 3D printers and run by Arduino microcontroller boards.

entries.name: Innovative Autonomous Haulage Vehicle
entries.def: Purpose built cabless mining haul truck with four wheel drive and four wheel steering that runs equally well in both directions without an operator station.
specs: Cabless chassis with four wheel drive, four wheel steering and retarder for bidirectional travel
Satellite positioning, radar, lidar and vehicle to vehicle communication under Komatsu's FrontRunner system
Fully driverless haulage supervised from a central control room
facts: Unveiled at MINExpo International 2016 in Las Vegas with a 230 tonne nominal payload
Measures about 15 metres long and 8.5 metres wide with a 15.9 metre turning radius
Komatsu's FrontRunner autonomous haulage system has been in commercial mine service on conventional trucks since 2008

entries.name: Insbot
entries.def: Robotic cockroach made in 2002 by researchers of the European LEURRE project to persuade real cockroaches to follow it, exploring natural pest control.
facts: Its predecessor, Alice, struggled because of its size and poor cockroach recognition
Carries more sensors and computing power than its predecessor

entries.name: Int-Ball
entries.maker: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency and University of Tokyo
entries.def: Ball shaped camera robot from the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency and the University of Tokyo that flies inside the ISS Kibō module, filming tasks to save crew time.
facts: Two different Int-Ball units had been delivered to the station by May 2024
Has a mass of about 1 kg

entries.name: Ion
entries.def: Robotic system from Intuitive that steers a thin flexible catheter deep into the lungs to take biopsies of small nodules.

entries.name: IRB 6
entries.def: Early industrial arm from ASEA, the forerunner of ABB, often described as the first all electric microprocessor controlled industrial robot.

entries.name: Iris
entries.def: Two kilogram student built lunar rover that flew on the Peregrine lander in January 2024 but never reached the Moon after the lander failed.

entries.name: iRobot Create
entries.def: Hobbyist robot made by iRobot from its Roomba vacuum platform, with the cleaning hardware replaced by a cargo bay for robotics development work.
facts: Introduced in 2007
Cargo bay holds a DB-9 port for serial data, input, output and power
Takes motor commands through the iRobot Roomba Open Interface protocol

entries.name: IRON
entries.def: Humanoid from a Chinese electric carmaker, built on automotive compute and battery technology with mass production targeted for late 2026.
specs: Electric joints with 22 degrees of freedom in the hands
Vehicle derived camera perception with indoor automatic emergency braking
Three in house Turing AI chips running a vision language action foundation model
facts: First shown at XPeng's 2024 technology day and substantially revised in November 2025
Uses a full solid state battery pack and three in house Turing AI chips
XPeng has stated a late 2026 start for mass production

entries.name: Isaac
entries.def: A folding home humanoid sold on preorder as a household assistant.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Weave Robotics

entries.name: IsaacRobot
entries.def: Two legged humanoid robot designed and built by the IsaacTeam, a student group at the Politecnico di Torino in Italy.
facts: Built by students of the Politecnico di Torino

entries.name: IXI-Play
entries.def: Android based robot companion for young children that read picture cards, mimicked the emotions on them, and ran games from its own app store.
facts: Announced with a retail price of $299
Designed to take swappable character skins

entries.name: Jackal
entries.def: A weatherproof compact research rover for field robotics.

entries.name: JACO
entries.def: Lightweight arm mounted on a power wheelchair so people with limited upper body mobility can eat, drink and open doors.

entries.name: Jason
entries.def: Two body remotely operated vehicle built and operated by the National Deep Submergence Laboratory of the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, first launched in 1988.
facts: Construction began in 1982
Rebuilt in 2002 as the second version of the vehicle
By 2020 it had completed 147 cruises, over 1,200 dives and over 16,000 dive hours

entries.name: Jason Jr.
entries.def: Small remotely operated vehicle built by the Deep Submergence Laboratory at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution as a test model for its bigger successor, Jason.
facts: Also known as JJ
Used to explore the wreck of the RMS Titanic
Its successor Jason was meant to work alongside the Argo camera sled

entries.name: JEMRMS
entries.def: Robotic arm system of the Japanese Kibo module on the International Space Station, used to move experiments onto the module's exposed platform.
facts: Pairs a main arm about 10 m long with a small fine arm for delicate work

entries.name: Jessiko
entries.def: Small autonomous robotic fish, 22 cm long, created by the French startup Robotswim, based in Palaiseau near Paris.
facts: Measures 22 cm (8.7 in) in length

entries.name: Jet Bot AI+
entries.def: Robot vacuum from Samsung that combines lidar with a 3D sensor and object recognition to avoid small obstacles.

entries.name: JetBot
entries.def: Open source robot kit built around an NVIDIA Jetson Nano computer, used to learn vision based navigation.

entries.name: Jia Jia
entries.maker: University of Science and Technology of China
entries.def: Lifelike female humanoid robot unveiled at the University of Science and Technology of China in 2016.

entries.name: Jibo
entries.def: Desktop social robot conceived by Cynthia Breazeal that turned its round head toward people as it talked.
facts: Its original servers were shut down in 2019 after the company sold its assets

entries.name: JO-ZERO
entries.def: Humanoid robot designed by manga artist Minoru Kamiya, creator of the anime Act On!, and manufactured by Himeji Softworks.
facts: Presented at the International Robot Exhibition in 2009

entries.name: Johns Hopkins Beast
entries.maker: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
entries.def: Early self sufficient mobile machine built in the 1960s at the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory that roamed corridors hunting for wall sockets to recharge itself.
facts: Found black power outlets along the lab's white halls and plugged itself in
Its simple onboard intelligence allowed it to fend for itself

entries.name: Jueying Lite3
entries.def: A parkour capable research quadruped in the consumer price class.

entries.name: Jueying X20
entries.def: A payload quadruped hauling sensors through disaster training rubble.

entries.name: Jueying X30
entries.def: An all weather inspection quadruped working power stations and tunnels.

entries.name: K10
entries.def: Family of prototype planetary rovers from NASA's Intelligent Robotics Group, with third generation units using four wheel drive and all wheel steering.
facts: Third generation units have a passive averaging suspension to reduce jolting on uneven ground
Mounting points front, back and bottom take antennas, sensors and instruments
Its controller runs on a Linux laptop linked by 802.11g or Tropos mesh wireless

entries.name: Kaikō
entries.def: Japanese deep sea remotely operated vehicle built by JAMSTEC that reached the floor of the Challenger Deep and was lost during a typhoon in 2003.
facts: Made more than 250 dives between 1995 and 2003
Collected 350 biological species from the deep sea
Lost off Shikoku on 29 May 2003 when a secondary cable snapped

entries.name: Kaleido
entries.def: Kawasaki's rugged full size humanoid, iterated yearly toward heavy field work.

entries.name: Kanguera
entries.def: Research robot hand from the University of São Paulo that models the kinematics of the human hand to help develop better humanlike grippers and manipulators.
facts: Runs the VxWorks operating system
Its name is an ancient indigenous word meaning bones outside the body

entries.name: Kärcher RC 3000
entries.def: Robotic vacuum cleaner made by Kärcher, notable for a docking station that emptied the dirt it collected into a paper bag.
facts: Introduced in 2002 and manufactured until January 2015
Its station let it keep running longer than other robot vacuums of the time

entries.name: Kaşif
entries.def: Remotely operated underwater vehicle from Turkey that supports subsea drilling by carrying out a range of tasks during offshore gas exploration.

entries.name: Kaspar
entries.def: Humanoid social robot developed at the University of Hertfordshire to act as a companion for autistic children and others who struggle with communication.

entries.name: Keepon
entries.def: Small yellow snowman shaped robot built for research on social interaction with autistic children, later sold as the dancing toy My Keepon.

entries.name: Kengoro
entries.def: A musculoskeletal humanoid that sweats through its frame to cool its motors while doing push ups.

entries.name: Kenshiro
entries.def: Musculoskeletal humanoid scaled to an average Japanese schoolboy and driven by about 160 tendon actuators arranged like human muscles.
specs: About 160 tendon driven artificial muscles with electric motors
Muscle tension sensing, joint angle sensing, inertial unit
facts: Roughly 160 tendon actuators standing in for human muscles
Anatomy modelled on an average twelve year old boy

refs.label: University of Tokyo JSK Laboratory website

entries.name: Kerfuś
entries.def: Autonomous delivery robot with a cartoon cat face used as Carrefour's store mascot in Poland, giving out snacks after its 2022 debut in Warsaw.
facts: Introduced in Warsaw stores in 2022
Launched as a joint Carrefour and PepsiCo advertising campaign
Went viral and turned into an internet meme

entries.name: KettyBot
entries.def: A slim ad screen waiter robot built for narrow café aisles.

entries.name: Khepera
entries.def: A matchbox research robot that made swarm experiments tabletop affairs.

entries.name: KHR-1
entries.def: Programmable two legged humanoid robot introduced by the Japanese firm Kondo Kagaku in 2004, when it ranked among the lowest priced robots of its type.
facts: Introduced in June 2004
34 cm tall with 17 degrees of freedom
Able to perform fast kung fu style combat moves

entries.name: KHR-3HV
entries.def: Hobby humanoid kit with seventeen servo joints, sold to enthusiasts and schools and long a standard machine in Japanese robot fighting leagues.
specs: 17 Kondo KRS series digital servo motors
Pre programmed motion sequences with radio control, edited in Kondo's HeartToHeart software
facts: A standard base machine in ROBO-ONE hobby humanoid fighting competitions
Sold as a self assembly kit through hobby distributors since 2009
Frame and servo layout designed to be modified and extended by owners

entries.name: Kilobot
entries.def: Low cost swarm robot from Harvard University that works in groups to perform tasks beyond a single unit, such as collective transport and self assembly into shapes.
facts: Stands 3.3 cm tall
Parts cost under $15 per robot
Created by Radhika Nagpal and Michael Rubenstein
In 2014 a swarm of 1,024 Kilobots arranged itself into shapes on command

entries.name: KINARM
aka: Kinesiological Instrument for Normal and Altered Reaching Movement
entries.def: Interactive robotic device that lets researchers measure how the brain handles sensing, movement and thinking through upper limb tasks, made by BKIN Technologies of Kingston, Ontario.
facts: Comes in two forms, the KINARM Exoskeleton and the KINARM End-Point
Used by basic and clinical researchers studying effects of injury and disease on the brain
Made by BKIN Technologies Ltd. in Kingston, Ontario

entries.name: Kirobo
entries.maker: University of Tokyo with Toyota, Dentsu and Robo Garage for JAXA
entries.def: Small talking humanoid flown to the International Space Station in 2013 to test conversation between an astronaut and a robot in orbit.
specs: Small servo motors in the head, arms and legs
Onboard speech recognition and dialogue with ground support
facts: First robot to hold a conversation with an astronaut in orbit
Holds two Guinness World Records for companion robot firsts in space

refs.label: University of Tokyo with Toyota, Dentsu and Robo Garage for JAXA website

entries.name: Kirobo Mini
entries.def: Compact robot developed by the Japanese company Toyota under the Kirobo Mini name.

entries.name: Kismet
entries.def: Expressive robot head created at MIT in the 1990s by Cynthia Breazeal as an affective computing experiment in reading and showing emotion.
facts: Built at MIT in the 1990s by Cynthia Breazeal
Name comes from a Turkish word meaning "fate" or "luck"

entries.name: Kiva Mobile Fulfillment System
entries.def: Squat orange drive unit that slides under portable inventory pods and carries them to human pick stations inside fulfillment centers.
specs: Differential drive chassis with a screw lift and rotating turntable for shelving pods
Rechargeable battery with automatic floor charging docks
Downward and upward barcode cameras, infrared obstacle sensors, contact bumpers
Central fleet server assigns tasks while robots follow a floor grid of barcode fiducials
hundreds of thousands of drive units
facts: First large deployments were at Staples and Walgreens distribution centers
Amazon acquired Kiva Systems for about 775 million dollars in 2012
The larger DU3000 variant could lift about 1,360 kg

refs.label: Wikipedia search, Kiva Mobile Fulfillment System

entries.name: Kiwibot
entries.def: Compact four wheeled campus and city delivery robot that carries food orders short distances, driving itself with human operators supervising and intervening remotely.
specs: Four wheeled electric drive with a top loading insulated bin
Rechargeable lithium battery, swapped or charged between shifts
Cameras, ultrasonic sensors and satellite positioning
Sidewalk autonomy backed by a remote operations centre that can drive the robot
facts: Announced with Sodexo a plan to bring more than a thousand robots to fifty college campuses
Runs campus delivery integrations with Grubhub dining accounts
Started as a student project at the University of California, Berkeley, with engineering in Medellin, Colombia; the company rebranded itself Robot.com in 2025

entries.name: KMR iiwa
entries.def: Omnidirectional mobile platform carrying a seven axis sensitive arm, used to move and load parts and samples in laboratories and factories.
specs: Omnidirectional Mecanum wheel platform with a seven axis LBR iiwa arm
Safety laser scanners plus joint torque sensing in every arm axis
Laser navigation on a stored map with docking for fine positioning
facts: Combines the torque sensing LBR iiwa arm with an omnidirectional base
Used for machine tending and laboratory sample handling

entries.name: Knightscope K5
entries.def: Outdoor autonomous security patrol robot that films, listens and reads licence plates while covering parking lots and campuses at pedestrian speed.
specs: Electric wheeled drive inside a sealed weatherproof shell
Battery electric with autonomous return to a charging pad
360 degree high definition cameras, thermal imaging, lidar, automatic licence plate recognition and two way audio
Autonomous patrol of mapped outdoor routes with alerts sent to human operators
facts: Patrols parking structures, corporate campuses and public spaces across the United States
The New York Police Department trialled a Knightscope robot on patrol duty
Knightscope also sells the four wheeled K7 for larger outdoor perimeters

entries.name: Kobian
entries.def: Humanoid robot developed at Waseda University in Japan that can show emotional expressions and was made to perform greetings suited to particular cultures.
facts: Can mimic human speech with lip movements and head oscillations

entries.name: Kodomoroid
entries.def: A child faced android newsreader on permanent duty at Tokyo's Miraikan museum.

entries.name: Kota the Triceratops
entries.def: Animatronic toy dinosaur in the form of a Triceratops that Hasbro and Playskool produced for children from 3 to 6 years old.
facts: Recommended age range of 3 to 6 years

entries.name: KR 1000 titan
entries.def: Heavy duty arm from KUKA rated for loads of about one tonne, used to move engine blocks, stone and glass.

entries.name: KR AGILUS
entries.def: Family of small, fast six axis arms from KUKA used in electronics and packaging lines.

entries.name: Kuavo
entries.def: A Harmony-OS-linked humanoid that performed at China's Spring Festival Gala.

entries.name: KUMO-I
entries.def: Spider inspired research quadruped by Shigeo Hirose and Yoji Umetani, the first machine in the long walking robot programme at Tokyo Institute of Technology.
specs: Electric motors driving hip and knee joints
facts: First machine in the Tokyo Institute of Technology line that became the TITAN series
Demonstrated omnidirectional walking without foot slip

entries.name: Kuri
entries.def: An adorable humming home robot cancelled weeks before mass shipment.

entries.name: Ladybird of Szeged
entries.def: Early Hungarian robot shaped like a red, black spotted ladybird, built at the University of Szeged to reproduce Pavlovian conditioned reflexes mechanically.
facts: Built between 1956 and 1957 by Dániel Muszka
Regarded as the earliest robotic animal
One of the first robots built in Hungary

entries.name: Laffing Sal
entries.def: Animatronic figure with a loud laugh, one of several characters built to lure carnival and amusement park visitors into funhouses and dark rides in the United States.
facts: Its laugh was known to scare young children and irritate adults

entries.name: Laikago
entries.def: First commercial quadruped from Unitree and the machine that opened the low cost Chinese robot dog market.
specs: In house brushless motors with planetary gear reduction
Onboard balance and gait control with a developer interface
facts: First quadruped sold commercially by a Chinese manufacturer
Founder Wang Xingxing developed its actuators from his university XDog prototype

entries.name: LAMA
entries.maker: Mobile Vehicle Engineering Institute and Laboratory for Analysis and Architecture of Systems
entries.def: French autonomous Mars rover prototype from 1990, developed by the Mobile Vehicle Engineering Institute and the Laboratory for Analysis and Architecture of Systems and weighing 300 kg.

entries.name: Land Walker
entries.def: Bipedal vehicle 3.4 m tall, invented by Masaaki Nagumo, that moves at about 1.5 km/h on wheels concealed under its feet rather than truly walking.
facts: Its creators hope similar machines might later serve in military and law enforcement roles

entries.name: Landroid
entries.def: Family of battery robot lawn mowers from Worx sold for home gardens.

entries.name: LaserWeeder
entries.def: Wide implement pulled behind a tractor that identifies weeds with cameras and kills them with high power lasers instead of chemicals or blades.
specs: Wheeled towed gantry with laser modules mounted over the crop bed
Camera arrays with onboard deep learning crop and weed classification
Automatic weed identification and laser targeting while towed; an optional autonomy kit drives the tractor
facts: The G2 line uses 240 watt lasers and spans working widths from about 6.6 feet to 60 feet
G2 units range from roughly 4,250 pounds for the narrowest model to 14,000 pounds for the widest
Used on commercial vegetable and specialty crop farms in the United States and Europe

entries.name: Laundroid
entries.def: Home robot that was meant to take clothes through washing, drying, ironing, sorting and folding automatically, promoted as the first machine of its kind.
facts: Sales were to begin in Japan, followed by a limited run in the United States
Release was set for 2017, with preorders from March 2017

entries.name: LAURON
entries.def: Six legged walking robot modelled on the stick insect Carausius morosus, developed over several generations by the German research centre FZI Forschungszentrum Informatik.
facts: First version shown to the public at CeBIT in Hanover in 1994
First generation relied on an artificial neural network for control
Fifth generation, LAURON V, was completed in 2013

entries.name: Lavo Bot
entries.def: Ground robot from Lucid Bots that pressure washes surfaces, launched to complement the company's Sherpa cleaning drone.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Lucid Bots

entries.name: LBR iiwa
entries.def: Seven axis lightweight arm from KUKA with torque sensors in every joint, developed from DLR research arms.
facts: Name stands for intelligent industrial work assistant

entries.name: LEGO Boost
entries.def: Building and coding set from LEGO with a motorised hub and a colour and distance sensor, used to make five starter robots.

entries.name: LEGO Education SPIKE Prime
entries.def: Classroom robotics set from LEGO Education built around a programmable hub with six ports for motors and sensors.

entries.name: Lego Mindstorms EV3
entries.def: Programmable robotics kit from the Lego Group, the third generation of the Mindstorms line, announced at CES in January 2013 and succeeding the NXT.
facts: Announced on 4 January 2013 at CES in Las Vegas
Reached shops on 1 September 2013; education edition on 1 August 2013
Used in contests such as FIRST LEGO League Challenge and World Robot Olympiad
LEGO retired the Mindstorms line at the end of 2022

entries.name: Lego Mindstorms NXT
entries.def: Robot building and programming kit from Lego, launched in August 2006 as the second generation of Mindstorms after the Robotics Invention System.
facts: Released on 2 August 2006
NXT 2.0 followed on 1 August 2009 with a color sensor
Succeeded by the third generation EV3 in September 2013

entries.name: LEGO Mindstorms RCX
entries.def: First LEGO Mindstorms programmable brick, which brought robot building with motors and sensors to children and hobbyists.
