facts: Grew out of a collaboration with the MIT Media Lab

entries.name: Lely Astronaut
entries.def: Milking robot from the Dutch firm Lely, in which cows walk in to be milked whenever they choose with no farmer present.
facts: The first Astronaut was installed on a farm in 1992

entries.name: Leonardo
entries.def: Social robot standing 2.5 feet tall, built by MIT's Personal Robots Group to study interaction and collaboration between humans and robots.
facts: Body built by Stan Winston Studios and completed in 2002
Created under the direction of Cynthia Breazeal
Named in Wired magazine's 50 Best Robots Ever list in 2006

entries.name: LEV-1
entries.def: Small hopping robot released from JAXA's SLIM lander in January 2024 that relayed pictures taken by its companion SORA-Q back to Earth.

entries.name: LeVO
entries.def: Autonomous pallet jack built by the American company Atlas Robotics to move pallets without a human operator.

entries.name: LeVO 3D
entries.def: Autonomous industrial truck that serves as a stacker and reach truck, part of the LeVO line from the American company Atlas Robotics.

entries.name: LeVO Double Fork
entries.def: Autonomous pallet jack with a double fork, a variant of the LeVO made by the American company Atlas Robotics.

entries.name: Lewis
entries.def: Autonomous robot photographer from the Media and Machines Laboratory at Washington University in St. Louis that roams social events taking pictures of guests.
facts: Built to do the job of a wedding photographer

entries.name: LG CLOi GuideBot
entries.def: Airport and lobby guide robot with a large touch screen that answers questions in several languages and escorts visitors to their destination.
specs: Rechargeable battery with about five hours to charge
Lidar, time of flight and depth cameras with bumper and magnetic sensors
Real time route planning with obstacle recognition on mixed floor surfaces
facts: First deployed as an airport guide at Incheon International Airport in 2017
Carries a 27 inch body touch display and a 9.2 inch face display
Launched with Korean and English, with more languages added later

entries.name: LG Roboking
entries.def: Line of robotic vacuum cleaners made by LG, sold as Roboking in Korea and under the Hom-Bot name in other markets.
facts: The first version was launched in 2001

entries.name: Lightweight Rover Unit
entries.maker: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics
entries.def: German four wheeled research rover used in Mount Etna campaigns to test autonomous lunar style survey and sample collection.
specs: Four wheels on actuated legs with independent steering
Battery electric with solar charging during field tests
Stereo cameras, inertial measurement, manipulator arm on one unit
Onboard stereo mapping, localisation and autonomous task execution
facts: Worked autonomously on Mount Etna in the ROBEX and ARCHES campaigns
Cooperated with a drone and relay link during analogue missions

refs.label: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics website

entries.name: LimX Oli
entries.def: Full size humanoid sold in tiered configurations from about 21,800 dollars, aimed at embodied intelligence research and commercial development work.
specs: Electric joint modules rated to 150 newton metres, 250 on the larger configuration
Head, chest and wrist depth cameras, IMU, optional lidar
Development platform with optional NVIDIA Orin NX perception compute
facts: Launched in July 2025 starting around 21,800 dollars
Offered in Lite, EDU and Super grades with 31 or 43 degrees of freedom
Optional NVIDIA Orin NX module adds about 157 trillion operations per second of perception compute

entries.name: Lingxi X1
entries.def: AgiBot's open source modular humanoid, released with drawings and code.

entries.name: Lingxi X2
entries.def: A nimble small humanoid that rides bicycles and skateboards in viral demonstrations.

entries.name: LittleDog
entries.def: Small electric quadruped supplied to university teams as the shared hardware of the DARPA Learning Locomotion programme.
specs: Electric geared motors, three joints per leg
Joint encoders, inertial sensing, external motion capture
Off board planning and control over a wireless link
facts: Common platform of the DARPA Learning Locomotion programme from 2006
Its rock field benchmark shaped modern footstep planning research

entries.name: Locus Origin
entries.def: Collaborative picking robot that carries totes to warehouse workers and shows pick instructions on a screen so people stay inside one zone.
specs: Lithium battery with about 50 minutes to a full charge
Lidar, cameras and an onboard barcode scanner
Map based navigation with dynamic path planning around people and obstacles
facts: Locus reported more than 10,000 robots across more than 250 sites by 2023
Customers include DHL, GEODIS, CEVA Logistics and Boots UK
Locus fleets passed one billion units picked in September 2022

entries.name: Lokomat
entries.def: Robotic gait trainer that moves a patient's legs over a treadmill while part of their body weight is supported by a harness.

entries.name: LOLA
entries.def: Munich research biped built for fast walking, with 25 actuated joints and a light structure that reached 3.34 km/h in experiments.
specs: Brushless motors in modular joint units
Six axis force and torque sensing in the feet, inertial unit, stereo vision
Real time walking pattern generation with vision based planning
facts: Walked at 3.34 km/h, among the faster European research bipeds
Successor to Johnnie in the Munich biped programme

entries.name: Looj
entries.def: Domestic robot made by the American consumer robot company iRobot, the firm behind the Roomba robotic vacuum cleaners.

entries.name: Loomo
entries.def: A hoverboard that transforms into a following robot companion.

entries.name: Loona
entries.def: A crowdfunded petbot that plays fetch and argues via a language model.

entries.name: LOVOT
entries.def: A warm bodied companion robot engineered solely to be loved.

entries.name: LR Mate 200iD
entries.def: Compact six axis arm from FANUC, one of the most widely installed small industrial robots.

entries.name: Luba AWD
entries.def: All wheel drive robot mower that navigates by satellite positioning instead of a boundary wire.

entries.name: LuckiBot
entries.def: A greeter and guide service robot leading guests to tables and rooms.

entries.name: Lucky the Dinosaur
entries.def: Roaming Disney animatronic figure of a green Segnosaurus, about 2.4 m tall, that hauls a cart decked in flowers while a handler leads it.
facts: Debuted at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles on 28 August 2003
Relocated to Hong Kong Disneyland for the park's opening in September 2005
Based at Walt Disney Imagineering as of August 2015, still meeting tour guests

entries.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
entries.def: NASA robotic spacecraft orbiting the Moon.

entries.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle
entries.maker: Boeing with General Motors Delco for NASA
entries.def: Battery powered four wheeled car driven by Apollo astronauts on the Moon, extending each crew's exploration range far beyond walking distance.
specs: Four wire mesh wheels with individual electric motors and front and rear steering
Sun compass, odometer and gyroscope driven navigation display
facts: Let Apollo crews work several kilometres from the lander
Apollo 17 crew drove about 36 km, the longest lunar traverse
All three vehicles remain on the Moon

refs.label: Boeing with General Motors Delco for NASA website

entries.name: Lunokhod 1
entries.def: First robotic rover to operate on another world, driving 10.5 kilometres across Mare Imbrium for the Soviet Luna 17 mission.
specs: Eight independently driven wheels with individual motors and brakes
Lid mounted solar panel with polonium 210 radioisotope heater
Two television cameras, four panoramic telephotometers, X ray spectrometer, penetrometer, laser retroreflector, radiation detector
Teleoperated from Earth with several seconds of command delay
facts: First remotely operated rover on another celestial body
Drove 10,540 metres over eleven lunar days
Held the lunar longevity record until Yutu-2 passed it in 2019

refs.label: NPO Lavochkin and VNII Transmash website

entries.name: Lunokhod 2
entries.def: Second Soviet lunar rover, delivered by Luna 21 to Le Monnier crater, which drove roughly 39 kilometres in under four months.
specs: Eight independently driven wheels with individual motors and brakes
Lid mounted solar panel with polonium 210 radioisotope heater
Three television cameras, panoramic telephotometers, boom mounted magnetometer, photodetector, solar X ray experiment, laser retroreflector
Teleoperated from Earth using television guidance
facts: Held the off world driving record for four decades
Agreed traverse of about 39 km, re estimated near 42 km from orbital imagery
Carried a French laser retroreflector still used for ranging

refs.label: NPO Lavochkin and VNII Transmash website

entries.name: Lunokhod 3
entries.def: Third generation Lunokhod completed in 1977 for a mission that was never funded, now preserved as a museum exhibit near Moscow.
specs: Lid mounted solar panel with radioisotope heater
Improved television and stereoscopic camera system
facts: Flight ready rover that never launched
Preserved intact at the NPO Lavochkin museum

refs.label: NPO Lavochkin and VNII Transmash website

entries.name: LUPEX rover
entries.def: Tracked lunar rover from Mitsubishi Heavy Industries of Japan for the Lunar Polar Exploration Mission, weighing 350 kg and measuring 2 m long.

entries.name: Luzi
entries.def: Individual Pepper robot given the name Luzi and operated by ZHB Luzern in Switzerland.

entries.name: Lynx
entries.def: A wheel legged all terrain machine that skates, walks and climbs.

entries.name: M-2000iA
entries.def: Very large six axis arm from FANUC that can lift car bodies and other loads weighing more than two tonnes.

entries.name: M1013
entries.def: Collaborative arm from Doosan Robotics with torque sensors in all six joints.

entries.name: MABEL
entries.maker: University of Michigan with Carnegie Mellon University
entries.def: Boom constrained biped at Michigan that used springs in series with its motors to run at 3.06 m/s, a record for a robot with knees.
specs: Electric motors with cable differentials and series springs
Hybrid zero dynamics feedback control, boom constrained to the sagittal plane
facts: Ran at 3.06 m/s in 2011, then the fastest for a knee equipped biped
Main experimental test bed for hybrid zero dynamics control

refs.label: University of Michigan with Carnegie Mellon University website
Wikidata, Michigan Anthropomorphic Biped With Electronic Legs (Q22095776)

entries.name: Maestro
entries.def: Pair of robotic arms from Moon Surgical that hold the camera and retract tissue for the surgeon during keyhole surgery.

entries.name: MAGGIE
aka: Mars Automated Giant Gizmo for Integrated Engineering
entries.def: Engineering test rover, its name short for Mars Automated Giant Gizmo for Integrated Engineering, used by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory as an Earth testbed for NASA's Curiosity rover.

entries.name: MagicBot
entries.def: A production line humanoid family also shown running and doing acrobatics.

entries.name: MAGPIE
entries.def: Lunar rover being developed by ispace for the European Space Agency to look for water ice near the Moon's south pole.
facts: Planned as the European Space Agency's first lunar rover mission
Due to launch in 2029 aboard ispace Mission 4

entries.name: MAHRU
entries.maker: Korea Institute of Science and Technology
entries.def: Humanoid robot developed by the Korea Institute of Science and Technology that draws its artificial intelligence from networks, created together with the related robot AHRA.
facts: Described as one of the first network based humanoids
Made public appearances in South Korea

refs.label: Korea Institute of Science and Technology website

entries.name: Mahru-Z
entries.maker: Korea Institute of Science and Technology
entries.def: KIST humanoid built for household chores, using three dimensional vision to recognise objects and operate appliances with its own hands and feet.
specs: Three dimensional vision system, force sensing feet
Recognises objects and sequences chores from high level commands
facts: Fourth generation of the KIST Mahru humanoid family
Demonstrated household chores including operating a microwave

refs.label: Korea Institute of Science and Technology website

entries.name: Mako
entries.def: Robotic arm system that guides surgeons cutting bone for knee and hip replacements according to a plan made from a CT scan.
facts: Stryker acquired the original maker, MAKO Surgical, in 2013

entries.name: Manav
entries.def: Humanoid robot developed in India, built with a body modelled on the human form.

entries.name: Manifold
entries.def: Drop in robotic labor from a 2026 Y Combinator company.

entries.name: Mantis
entries.def: Autonomous robot from the American company Atlas Robotics that works as a pallet jack and can also pick individual cases.

entries.name: MAPP
entries.def: Commercial prospecting rover carrying a cellular network demonstration to the Moon, stranded aboard the IM-2 lander after it tipped over.
specs: Four wheel drive platform with payload deck
Navigation cameras with customer payload interfaces
Semi autonomous driving under ground supervision
facts: Carried the first cellular network node sent to the Moon
Never deployed because the IM-2 lander toppled

entries.name: Marble
entries.def: Sidewalk delivery robot tested in San Francisco, whose maker was acquired by Caterpillar in 2020.

entries.name: Marie Curie
entries.def: Flight spare twin of the Sojourner microrover, built for Mars Pathfinder and later used for engineering work before museum preservation.
specs: Six independently driven wheels on a rocker bogie chassis
Solar array with primary lithium batteries
Three cameras and laser stripe hazard detection
facts: Identical twin of the first rover to drive on Mars
Never flew and is held in the Smithsonian collection

entries.name: Mariner 4
entries.def: Robotic spacecraft sent by NASA to Mars.

entries.name: Mark II
entries.def: Rideable robot controlled by its riders, made by the US company MegaBots and first shown at Maker Faire San Mateo in May 2015.
facts: Upgrade for melee combat announced in August 2015 to take on Kuratas
Upgrade funding came from a Kickstarter campaign
Successor Mk.III was scheduled to fight Kuratas in August 2017

entries.name: Marsokhod
entries.def: Soviet designed six wheeled rover chassis used in Russian, French and American field trials at volcanoes and deserts through the 1990s.
specs: Three articulated segments, each with a pair of driven conical wheels
Battery electric with solar options in some trials
Stereo cameras, imaging mast and campaign specific science payloads
facts: Flexing chassis can climb obstacles larger than its wheels
Used in joint Russian, French and American analogue field tests

entries.name: Marty
entries.def: Grey tower robot with googly eyes that roams supermarket aisles looking for spills and hazards and checking shelves for stock and price errors.
specs: Wheeled base with a tall sensor mast
Cameras and lidar with floor facing hazard detection
Map based navigation among shoppers with automatic alerts to staff
facts: Nearly 500 units rolled out across Giant, Martin's and Stop and Shop stores in 2019
Stop and Shop upgraded Marty units at more than 300 locations in 2023
Reported accuracy of about 95 percent on out of stock detection by one customer

entries.name: Marvin
aka: Mobile Autonomous Robot Vehicle for Indoor Navigation
entries.def: Indoor mobile research robot from the Robotics Lab at the University of Kaiserslautern, using laser scanners, ultrasonic sensors and a camera to navigate and map rooms.
facts: Name stands for Mobile Autonomous Robot Vehicle for Indoor Navigation
Uses a differential drive and a behaviour based control system
Has a stereo microphone system to locate sound sources

entries.name: MASCOT
entries.def: Shoebox sized lander carried by Hayabusa2 that used an internal swinging arm to hop across asteroid Ryugu in 2018.
facts: Worked for about 17 hours on its battery

entries.name: Matic
entries.def: A camera only home vacuum that maps like a self driving car and keeps data on device.

entries.name: Maurice
entries.def: Small home robot from Innate with a single arm, designed to be taught new chores through code, language and demonstration.

entries.name: Max
entries.def: Wheel legged quadruped from Tencent's robotics laboratory that switches between walking on four legs and rolling on wheels.
specs: Electric joint actuators with a driven wheel on each leg
Onboard hybrid locomotion control with fall recovery
facts: Combines legged and wheeled locomotion in one machine, switching modes on the move
Announced in March 2021 as Tencent Robotics X's first self developed quadruped

entries.name: Maya AUV
entries.def: Indian autonomous underwater vehicle built by the marine instrumentation team at the National Institute of Oceanography.

entries.name: Mazor X
entries.def: Robotic guidance system for spine surgery from Mazor Robotics, which Medtronic acquired in 2018.

entries.name: mBot
entries.def: Line of toy robot kits for children made by the Chinese company Makeblock.

entries.name: Meca500
entries.def: Very small six axis industrial arm from Mecademic, sized for laboratory automation and electronics assembly.

entries.name: Meccanoid
entries.def: Buildable humanoid robot kit from Meccano that learns movements by recording poses its owner moves it through.

entries.name: Mech
entries.def: A twin armed industrial superhumanoid on a lifting base, built for truck loading in heat and cold.

entries.name: Mechanical Turk
entries.def: Hoax chess automaton built by Wolfgang von Kempelen whose apparent skill came from a chess master concealed inside, moving the pieces with levers and magnets.
facts: First displayed in 1770
Toured as an automaton for 84 years before a fire destroyed it in 1854
Its secret was fully explained in an 1857 article by the owner's son

entries.name: Meinü robot
entries.def: Female humanoid robot from China, reported by Chinese news outlets in 2006, whose Mandarin name is officially rendered in English as beauty robot.
facts: The Mandarin name literally means beautiful woman robot
The first Meinü robot was later given the name Miss Rong Cheng

entries.name: MEISTeR
aka: Maintenance Equipment Integrated System of Telecontrol Robot
entries.def: Remotely controlled maintenance robot from Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, built for work inside the damaged Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant.
facts: Name stands for Maintenance Equipment Integrated System of Telecontrol Robot

entries.name: Melody (Aria)
entries.def: A modular companion android with swappable faces, sold for connection rather than labour.

entries.name: MenteeBot
entries.def: A household and warehouse humanoid trained end to end on language to motion models.

entries.name: Mephisto
entries.def: Chess playing machine passed off as an automaton, built in London by Charles Godfrey Gumpel, an Alsatian maker of artificial limbs, and first exhibited in 1878.
facts: Took six or seven years to build
Its first showing took place at Gumpel's Leicester Square home

entries.name: Mezli
entries.def: Fully automated restaurant built into a shipping container that cooked meals for takeout and delivery.

entries.name: Mi Robot Vacuum
entries.def: Laser mapping robot vacuum sold by Xiaomi and made by Roborock, which brought lidar navigation to a low price.

entries.name: Michelangelo Hand
entries.def: Robotic prosthetic hand with full articulation made by the German company Ottobock with its American partner Advanced Arm Dynamics, the first prosthesis with an electronically driven thumb.
facts: First fitted to an Austrian elective amputee in July 2010
Used by military and civilian amputees in the United States and United Kingdom since 2011
Its thumb movement imitates that of a natural human hand

entries.name: Milo
entries.def: Small expressive humanoid robot used to teach social and emotional skills to children with autism.

entries.name: Mindar
entries.def: Android at the Kōdai-ji Zen temple in Kyoto that preaches regularly on the Heart Sutra and was made to personify Kannon, the bodhisattva of compassion.
facts: Serves at Kōdai-ji in Kyoto, a Zen temple with 400 years of history
Also called Android Kannon Mindar

entries.name: MINERVA
entries.def: Series of Japanese rovers built by JAXA to explore the surfaces of asteroids, carried on the Hayabusa and Hayabusa2 missions.
facts: First MINERVA missed asteroid Itokawa in November 2005 and drifted into solar orbit
Two MINERVA-II rovers landed on asteroid Ryugu on 21 September 2018
Third MINERVA-II unit malfunctioned but was released in October 2019 for gravity measurements

refs.label: Wikidata, Micro-Nano Experimental Robot Vehicle for Asteroid (Q17231034)

entries.name: MINERVA-II1
entries.def: Pair of small rovers released by Hayabusa2 onto asteroid Ryugu in 2018, the first rovers to move across the surface of an asteroid, which they did by hopping.

entries.name: Mini Cheetah
entries.def: Nine kilogram electric quadruped built from modular actuators, the first four legged robot shown performing a backflip.
specs: Onboard model predictive and learned controllers
facts: First quadruped robot to perform a backflip
Its open documentation and modular actuator design were widely copied in low cost quadrupeds

entries.name: Mini Pupper
entries.def: A ROS native open source desktop quadruped crowdfunded by hobbyists.

entries.name: Mini Pupper 2
entries.def: Small open source quadruped kit built around a Raspberry Pi and ROS 2, aimed at students learning navigation and mapping.
specs: Camera, optional two dimensional lidar, inertial measurement unit
ROS 2 stack with mapping and navigation on a Raspberry Pi
facts: Crowdfunded in late 2022 and supplied as an open source ROS 2 teaching kit
Derived from the openly published Stanford Pupper design

entries.name: Mini Rover ROV
entries.def: Tethered underwater remotely operated vehicle created by Chris Nicholson of Deep Sea Systems International, introduced in 1983 as the first compact and inexpensive ROV.
facts: Launched at $26,850 when the next cheapest ROV cost $100,000
First unit built in Nicholson's garage in Falmouth, Massachusetts
26 inches long and 55 pounds, small enough to travel as airline luggage

entries.name: Minitaur
entries.def: A springy direct drive quadruped that climbed fences and opened doors on legs alone.

entries.name: Minsky's Tentacle Arm
entries.def: Robot arm dating from 1965, built to imitate a human arm and now exhibited at the MIT Museum.

entries.name: MiP
entries.def: Self balancing toy robot that rides on two wheels, carries a small tray and responds to hand gestures.

entries.name: MiPA
entries.def: A wheeled household and care humanoid intended for serial production in Europe.

entries.name: MiR250
entries.def: Low profile 250 kg autonomous mobile robot for factories and hospitals, built to slide under carts and shelves or carry custom top modules.
specs: Lithium battery with an optional swap pack
Two safety laser scanners, two 3D cameras and eight proximity sensors
Laser SLAM with fleet management and marker docking to about 3 mm
facts: Docks to marker positions with roughly 3 mm repeatability
Sold with pallet lift, shelf lift and conveyor top modules
Part of the Teradyne robotics group alongside Universal Robots

entries.name: MiRo
entries.def: Social robot made by the British company Consequential Robotics, intended to interact and communicate with people.

entries.name: Mirokai
entries.def: Character styled service robot that balances on a single ball, trialled in Paris hospitals for carrying samples, linens and small deliveries.
specs: Ball balancing single sphere drive with two electric arms
Depth cameras, lidar, microphone array, animated face display
Autonomous indoor navigation with remote operator assistance
facts: Trialled in Paris hospitals for internal transport of samples and supplies
Ball balancing drive lets it turn on the spot in narrow corridors
Designed as a stylised fictional character rather than a human likeness

entries.name: Misty II
entries.def: A developer platform desk robot with a programmable personality.

entries.name: MIT Cheetah 2
entries.def: Electric bounding quadruped that ran untethered on grass and jumped hurdles, built to show motors could match hydraulics.
specs: Custom high torque density brushless motors with low gear ratio transmissions
Joint encoders, inertial measurement unit, lidar for obstacle detection
Impulse based bounding control with onboard obstacle jumping planner
facts: Bounded at 6.4 m/s, among the fastest speeds recorded for an electric quadruped
First four legged robot to detect and jump over obstacles autonomously while running
Its proprioceptive actuator concept shaped later MIT and commercial quadrupeds

entries.name: MIT Cheetah 3
entries.def: Forty kilogram electric quadruped that climbed cluttered stairs and jumped onto tables using only proprioception, with no cameras.
specs: Proprioceptive brushless motors with low gear ratio transmissions
Inertial measurement unit and joint encoders only
Model predictive control with contact detection and no exteroceptive sensing
facts: Climbed stairs littered with obstacles with no vision at all
Its control software became the basis of the open source stack used on Mini Cheetah

entries.name: MIT Quadruped
entries.def: Hydraulic running quadruped from Marc Raibert's MIT Leg Laboratory that trotted, paced and bounded using a decomposed balance controller.
specs: Off board hydraulic supply through a tether
Off board computer running decomposed balance control
facts: Demonstrated trot, pace and bound gaits with active balance on a machine that ran rather than walked
Marc Raibert, who led the work, founded Boston Dynamics in 1992

entries.name: MIT-Manus
entries.def: Arm rehabilitation robot from MIT that guides a patient's hand through reaching exercises after stroke, later sold under the InMotion name.

entries.name: Mitra
entries.def: Humanoid robot from Bangalore startup Invento Robotics that made its debut at the Global Entrepreneurship Summit in November 2017, where it welcomed Ivanka Trump.
facts: Debuted in November 2017 at the Global Entrepreneurship Summit
Greeted Ivanka Trump and interacted with Prime Minister Narendra Modi
Invento Robotics was founded in Bangalore by Balaji Viswanathan

entries.name: Mobot
entries.def: Mechanical robots that tap and swipe real phones to test mobile apps where emulators fall short.

entries.name: Modulus
entries.def: Domestic robot developed from 1984 by Sirius, a company founded by Massimo Giuliana, with an exterior designed by the Milan based Japanese designer Isao Hosoe.
facts: Electronics and mechanics were designed and made by Data Process
Software was written with help from the US based RB Robot Corporation

entries.name: Moflin
entries.def: Furry palm sized companion robot that develops its own character as it responds to touch and voice.

entries.name: Molecubes
entries.def: Modular robot system from Cornell University made of cubes with two rotating halves that can be joined together into many different shapes.
facts: Designed by Hod Lipson, Victor Zykov and Stathis Mytilinaios
One half of each cube holds a microprocessor, the other a motor

entries.name: Moley Robotic Kitchen
entries.def: Pair of ceiling mounted arms with dexterous hands that cook recipes recorded from human chefs.
facts: Prototype first shown in 2015

entries.name: Momaro
entries.def: Centaur like robot from the University of Bonn with four legs ending in wheels and two arms, built for the DARPA Robotics Challenge.
facts: Finished fourth in the 2015 DARPA Robotics Challenge finals

entries.name: Mona
entries.def: A whimsical care focused humanoid designed for homes rather than factories.

refs.label: TechCrunch, Kind Humanoid and Yves Behar

entries.name: Monarch
entries.def: Robotic platform for bronchoscopy developed by Auris Health, which Johnson and Johnson acquired in 2019.

entries.name: Monarch MK-V
entries.def: Battery electric compact utility tractor with driver optional autonomy, sold for vineyards, orchards and dairies, with cameras for row following and safety.
specs: Four wheel drive battery electric tractor with a category one and two three point hitch
Battery electric with 5.6 kilowatts of exportable power
360 degree camera coverage with collision prevention and power take off protection
Driver optional operation with row following and gesture control; one operator can supervise up to eight tractors
facts: Rated 40 horsepower continuous and 70 horsepower peak, with a 14 hour working day on a charge
Assembled in Livermore, California, with a manufacturing partnership with Foxconn in Ohio
Widely used in California wine grape vineyards and on dairies

entries.name: MoonRanger
entries.def: Suitcase sized autonomous lunar rover built to scout hundreds of metres from its lander without waiting for driving commands.
specs: Four wheel drive with independent motors
Flip up solar panel with battery
Fully autonomous waypoint navigation with onboard mapping
facts: Built to navigate autonomously beyond radio contact with its lander
Scheduled to fly on a Blue Ghost lander in 2029

refs.label: Carnegie Mellon University and Astrobotic website

entries.name: Morphle
entries.def: Robotic microscopes from Bengaluru that automate slide scanning for cancer diagnostics.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Morphle Labs

entries.name: Motoman HC10
entries.def: Collaborative arm in the Yaskawa Motoman range with hand guided teaching and pinch point protection.

entries.name: Moxi
entries.def: Hospital service robot with a single arm and an expressive head, leased to health systems to fetch and deliver supplies for nurses.
specs: Single seven degree of freedom arm on an omnidirectional wheeled base
Onboard rechargeable battery with automatic docking
Lidar, depth cameras and a socially expressive LED eye display
Autonomous corridor navigation with networked lift and door control plus remote human fallback
facts: Deployed across multiple United States hospital systems on a subscription model
Uses networked control to ride lifts and open supply room doors unaided
Texas Health Resources was among its first large health system customers

entries.name: Moxie
entries.def: Companion robot developed and produced by the company Embodied and later discontinued.

entries.name: Multiply Labs
entries.def: Cloud controlled modular robotic system that manufactures individualized drugs, a process normally done by hand.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Multiply Labs

entries.name: Muppet Mobile Lab
entries.def: Free roving animatronic attraction created by Walt Disney Imagineering and trialled at Disney theme parks in Anaheim, Orlando and Hong Kong.
facts: Tested at Disney California Adventure, Walt Disney World and Hong Kong Disneyland

entries.name: Murata Boy and Murata Girl
entries.def: Pair of self balancing robots built by Japanese electronic components maker Murata Manufacturing to demonstrate its products and attract publicity.
facts: Designed to use as little energy as possible
Include an automatic sleep mode to save power

refs.label: Wikipedia, Murata Boy and Murata Girl
Wikidata, Murata Boy and Murata Girl (Q18378299)

entries.name: MUSA
entries.def: Kendo fighting robot completed in July 2005 by the Manufacturing and Mechatronics Lab of Seoul National University under Professor Young-Bong Bang.
facts: Stands 163 cm tall and weighs 70 kg

entries.name: Musio
entries.def: Social robot from AKA Intelligence that converses with people to help them practise spoken English, recognising objects, reading facial expressions and showing expressions of its own.
facts: Runs on MUSE, an AI engine built for conversation
Raised 201% of its goal, just over $100k, on Indiegogo in May 2015

entries.name: myCobot 280
entries.def: Palm sized six axis arm from Elephant Robotics sold for teaching and hobby projects.

entries.name: Myon
entries.maker: Humboldt University of Berlin, Neurorobotics Research Laboratory
entries.def: Modular humanoid from Berlin whose limbs can be detached and keep working, built for research on distributed neural style control.
specs: Modular electric actuator units, one set per body part
Distributed neural style control across per limb processing nodes
facts: Limbs can be removed and continue operating on their own power
Performed in the opera My Square Lady at the Komische Oper Berlin

refs.label: Humboldt University of Berlin, Neurorobotics Research Laboratory website

entries.name: Mytos
entries.def: Robotic platform that turns stem cells into specific cell types such as neurons and heart cells over several weeks.

entries.name: N1
entries.def: An open source compact humanoid released with full build files.

entries.name: N2
entries.def: A knee high acrobatic biped that finished second in Beijing's robot marathon.

entries.name: Nadia
entries.def: A boxing trained research humanoid with human like range of motion, built with Boardwalk.

entries.name: Nadine
entries.def: Lifelike female humanoid social robot whose looks are based on Professor Nadia Magnenat Thalmann, able to recognise people, remember past conversations and answer questions in several languages.
facts: Its face and upper body have 27 degrees of freedom in total
Can serve as an office receptionist or a personal coach

entries.name: NAO
entries.def: Small programmable biped sold in large numbers to schools, universities and research labs, and long the standard platform for RoboCup soccer leagues.
specs: Two cameras, four microphones, sonar, infrared, tactile and pressure sensors, IMU
NAOqi framework with Choregraphe, Python and ROS interfaces
facts: About 20,000 units sold, largely into education and research
Fixed platform of the RoboCup Standard Platform League for many years
Maker Aldebaran filed for bankruptcy in February 2025 and entered receivership in June 2025

entries.name: Navel
entries.def: Social robot developed by the German company navel robotics for use in care facilities.

entries.name: Navibot
entries.def: Robot vacuum from Samsung that worked out its position by photographing the ceiling with an upward facing camera.

entries.name: Navimow
entries.def: Wire free robotic lawn mower that uses satellite positioning to stay inside a mapped area, aimed at residential lawns in Europe and North America.
specs: Two driven wheels with a rear caster and a rotating blade disc
Lithium battery with an automatic charging base
Satellite positioning with a reference antenna, plus cameras for obstacle recognition on later models
Wire free autonomous mowing inside app defined virtual boundaries and zones
facts: Launched in Europe in 2021 as one of the first mainstream wire free robotic mowers
Uses a satellite reference station mounted on the house or a pole for centimetre level positioning
Built by Segway, better known for self balancing personal transporters and scooters

entries.name: NeCoRo
entries.def: Robot built in the form of an animal and sold as a product by the Japanese company Omron.

entries.name: Neo
entries.def: Self driving floor scrubbing machine for large indoor sites that maps a building once and then repeats cleaning routes without an operator.
specs: Scrubber deck with separate solution and recovery tanks on a self driving chassis
Lidar and 3D cameras giving 360 degree coverage
Maps a site once, then repeats stored cleaning plans with dynamic obstacle avoidance
facts: Deployed at Changi Airport, Narita International Airport and Montreal Trudeau
Also sold as the Neo 2W, with a smaller Kas model for tight spaces
Avidbots was founded in Kitchener, Ontario in 2014

entries.name: NEO
entries.def: Soft bodied household humanoid sold for early access delivery from 2026, with a tendon drive and optional remote human operation for unfamiliar chores.
specs: Tendon drive transmitting from high torque density electric motors
Head and body cameras with microphone array
Onboard vision and speech models with scheduled human teleoperation fallback
facts: Preorders opened in October 2025 at 20,000 dollars or a 499 dollar monthly subscription
Rated at 22 decibels of operating noise for household use
First United States home deliveries promised for 2026, other markets from 2027

entries.name: Neo 2
entries.def: A self driving floor scrubber mapping airports and malls each night.

entries.name: Neolix X3
entries.def: Low speed cabless electric delivery van used for parcels, groceries and vending on Chinese public roads under Level 4 autonomy with remote supervision.
specs: Cabless four wheeled low speed electric vehicle with a modular cargo body
Battery electric drive with swappable battery packs
SAE Level 4 map free navigation on public roads with remote supervision
facts: Neolix reports more than 10,000 RoboVans deployed in 300 cities across 15 countries
Fleet has covered more than 50 million kilometres, with over 1,200 units in Qingdao alone
Founded in 2018 and among the first Chinese firms to mass produce driverless delivery vehicles

entries.name: Nereus
entries.def: Hybrid uncrewed underwater vehicle from the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, made for research at full ocean depth, which reached the floor of the Challenger Deep in 2009.
facts: Rated to operate as deep as 11,000 metres
Reached the bottom of the Challenger Deep on 31 May 2009
Name chosen through a nationwide student contest

entries.name: NeuroArm
entries.def: Research robot for neurosurgery, the first image guided surgical robot compatible with magnetic resonance imaging that can carry out both microsurgery and stereotaxy.
facts: First image guided, MR compatible surgical robot able to do microsurgery and stereotaxy

entries.name: Neuromorphic
entries.def: Mobile robot that moves between wet lab benches and operates existing scientific instruments like a technician.

entries.name: Nexi
entries.def: Mobile, dexterous and social robot from the MIT Media Lab Personal Robots Group, with an expressive face on a self balancing wheeled base.

entries.name: NEXTAGE
entries.def: Dual arm humanoid torso sold for precision cell production, working at benches alongside people in electronics and precision assembly plants.
specs: Electric servo joints in two six axis arms, a two axis head and a rotating waist
Stereo head cameras and hand mounted cameras for part location
Task programming with vision based part detection and workstation calibration
facts: Designed to occupy human workstations without re tooling the production line
Sold for electronics assembly, inspection and machine tending in Japan and abroad
Grew out of Kawada's earlier humanoid platform engineering

entries.name: NICOBO
entries.def: A shy tail wagging cushion robot that speaks in half formed words.

entries.name: Nomad
entries.def: Car sized Carnegie Mellon field rover that drove 215 kilometres across the Atacama Desert and later searched Antarctica for meteorites.
specs: Four wheel drive and four wheel steering on an expanding chassis
Panoramic imaging mast, stereo cameras, spectrometer and metal detector for meteorite work
Mostly teleoperated with autonomous navigation segments
facts: Drove 215 km in 45 days across the Atacama Desert
First robot to autonomously identify a meteorite, in Antarctica in 2000

entries.name: Nomad 200
entries.def: Commercial mobile robot made by Nomadic Technologies in the 1990s, with a choice of sensors, chiefly for robotics lab courses and research and development.
facts: Also known as the N200
Manufactured in the 1990s by Nomadic Technologies, Inc.

entries.name: Nori
entries.def: American made humanoid announced at a price of $1,688.

entries.name: Nova 5
entries.def: Autonomous search and rescue robot created by engineer brothers Fady and Sami Khaled that uses a fuzzy neural network to make sense of its surroundings and find its own way.
facts: Navigates on its own rather than by remote control
Runs a built in fuzzy neural network modelled on brain neurons

entries.name: Nuro R2
entries.def: Cabless road going electric delivery pod with no seats or steering wheel, used for grocery and pizza delivery in Texas, Arizona and California.
specs: Purpose built cabless low speed electric vehicle with two goods compartments
Lidar, radar, thermal cameras and a 360 degree camera array
Driverless Level 4 operation on public roads with remote fleet monitoring
facts: Received the first federal exemption granted to a driverless vehicle in the United States in February 2020
Delivered for Kroger, Domino's, Walmart and CVS in Houston, Phoenix and the Bay Area
Nuro pivoted in September 2024 to licensing its autonomous driving system, ending its own delivery service

entries.name: Nuum
entries.def: Snake like robot that travels inside machinery to inspect and maintain it.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Nuum Robotics

entries.name: Ocado 600 Series Bot
entries.def: Grid running grocery picking robot from Ocado, much lighter than its predecessors and built partly from 3D printed parts.

entries.name: Ocean Aero Triton
entries.def: Autonomous vessel from the American company Ocean Aero that can travel both on the surface and underwater, propelled by solar and wind power for long missions.
facts: As of 2026 the only naval drone able to operate autonomously both surfaced and submerged
Mass of 350 kg and length of 4.5 m

entries.name: OceanOneK
entries.def: A haptic humanoid diver that explores shipwrecks a kilometre down while its pilot feels what it touches.

entries.name: Octobot
entries.def: Autonomous robot made of soft materials, built by a Harvard University team to show the approach could work and described in Nature in 2016.
facts: Team included Harvard faculty Robert Wood and Jennifer A. Lewis
Drew on mechanical engineering, 3D printing and microfluidics

entries.name: Odin
entries.def: Robot arms placed in small and mid sized factories for machine tending and packing, working beside existing machines and people.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Odin Robotics

entries.name: OhmniCare
entries.def: Telepresence robot for clinics and care homes with a tall touchscreen and four cameras, driven by a remote clinician from a browser.
specs: Four wheel base with 30 W brushless motors and six inch wheels
Rechargeable battery with up to 18 hours of standby
Four cameras including 4K front, rear and downward views
facts: Replaced the original Ohmni telepresence robot, discontinued in 2024
Carries a 21.5 inch high definition touchscreen

entries.name: Omnibot
entries.def: Toy robot first made by Tomy in the mid 1980s, whose name later covered a whole line of the company's robots.
facts: The more advanced Omnibot 2000 had no plastic dome over its head
The line faded after the 1983 video game crash and returned in the early 2000s
Its most recent version is the i-SOBOT

entries.name: OmniTread
entries.def: Segmented serpentine robot covered in moving treads on all sides, so it can push through rubble whichever way it lands.

entries.name: OMRON LD-250
entries.def: Industrial autonomous mobile robot that carries 250 kg of parts between machines and stores using laser mapping instead of floor tape or magnets.
specs: Lithium ion battery with autonomous docking
Safety rated laser scanners and time of flight obstacle sensors
Onboard SLAM with a fleet manager coordinating traffic and charging
facts: Descends from the Adept Lynx platform OMRON acquired in 2015
Runs about 13 hours unloaded and 10 hours at full payload

entries.name: Opentrons Flex
entries.def: Larger successor to the OT-2 launched in May 2023, adding a gripper that moves labware between deck positions.

entries.name: Opportunity
entries.def: Twin of Spirit that landed in Meridiani Planum, confirmed water altered bedrock and drove 45 kilometres over more than fourteen years.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive with four corner steering
Solar arrays with rechargeable lithium ion batteries
Panoramic and navigation cameras, microscopic imager, alpha particle X ray and Moessbauer spectrometers, rock abrasion tool
Ground planned drives with autonomous navigation and visual odometry
facts: Holds the off Earth driving record for a wheeled vehicle at 45.16 km
First rover to complete a marathon distance on another planet
Found haematite spherules and sulphate rocks laid down in liquid water

entries.name: OPTIMISM
entries.def: Full scale Earth twin of Perseverance kept in JPL's Mars Yard to rehearse drives and debug problems with the flight rover.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive matching the flight rover
Mains or battery supply during yard testing
Flight like cameras, robotic arm and coring hardware
Runs flight software builds to rehearse autonomous drives
facts: Used to reproduce and solve the 2022 sample tube pebble jam
Full scale twin that rehearses every complex rover activity

entries.name: Optimus
entries.def: Full size electric humanoid that Tesla is developing for factory and general labour tasks, currently used only inside Tesla facilities.
specs: Custom rotary and linear electric actuators with an 11-degree of freedom hand
2.3 kWh battery pack housed in the torso
Camera based vision with tactile fingertip sensing
End to end neural network policies sharing perception software with Tesla's driver assistance stack
facts: Walked unassisted on stage at Tesla AI Day in September 2022
Second generation announced in December 2023 with reduced mass and faster walking
Shown handling parts inside Tesla manufacturing sites and serving food at a company diner

entries.name: Orangewood Labs
entries.def: San Francisco maker of low cost robot arms and the software that lets them learn new tasks.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Orangewood Labs

entries.name: Orb Swarm
entries.def: Kinetic art piece made up of six partly autonomous spherical robots, built in 2007 by engineers and artists to imitate natural swarms and human dance.
facts: Consists of six spherical robots
Created in 2007 by a team including Michael Prados, Jon Foote and Lee Sonko
Nearly all of its hardware and software is open source

entries.name: Origami hand
entries.def: High degree of freedom direct drive robotic hand from Origami Robotics, matched to a glove like device that records human demonstrations.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Origami Robotics

entries.name: OS3
entries.def: Low cost mobile humanoid designed and built in the United States by a two person team.

entries.name: OT-2
entries.def: Benchtop pipetting robot from Opentrons with an open source protocol library, built to bring lab automation to ordinary biology labs.

refs.label: Wikidata, Opentrons OT-2 liquid handling bot (Q115147895)

entries.name: Otonaroid
entries.def: Adult female android by Hiroshi Ishiguro, shown with Kodomoroid at Tokyo's Miraikan science museum in 2014.

entries.name: OTTO 1500
entries.def: Heavy duty self driving vehicle for factories that moves pallets and large assemblies weighing up to 1,900 kg without floor guidance.
specs: Safety lidar, four depth cameras and a six axis inertial unit
Lidar SLAM with fleet manager traffic control and no floor infrastructure
facts: Grew out of Clearpath Robotics and was acquired by Rockwell Automation in 2023
Heavy class OTTO robots passed one million production hours
Turns in place with a maximum turning speed of 1.5 rad per second

entries.name: Ottobot
entries.def: An airport and curbside delivery robot rolling through terminals in several countries.

entries.name: Oz
entries.def: Small electric tool carrier that weeds, sows and marks rows in market garden beds, driving itself between crop rows using satellite guidance.
specs: Four wheeled electric drive tool carrier with a maximum working width of one metre
Lithium battery giving up to eight hours of work
Autonomous row work guided by corrected satellite positioning, with obstacle detection and emergency stop
facts: More than 35 compatible implements are offered for weeding, sowing and row marking
Naio also builds the larger Dino for vegetable beds and Ted for vineyards
Aimed at market gardening and aromatic plant growers working small plots

entries.name: Ozobot
entries.def: Tiny line following robot that reads coloured codes drawn on paper or a screen, used to teach coding in schools.

entries.name: P3
entries.def: Honda's first fully self contained walking humanoid, ancestor of ASIMO.

entries.name: P800
entries.def: The flagship of China's largest AMR fleet, moving shelves in hundreds of warehouses.

entries.name: PALRO
entries.def: Small humanoid communication robot used to lead games and exercises in Japanese care homes for the elderly.

entries.name: Panda
entries.def: Seven axis arm with torque sensing in every joint, sold at a low price and widely adopted by research laboratories.
facts: Its designers received the German Future Prize in 2017
Succeeded by the Franka Research 3

entries.name: PaPeRo
entries.def: Personal robot developed by the Japanese firm NEC, known for its endearing appearance and facial recognition, with work starting in 1997 on the R100 prototype.
facts: Development began in 1997 with the R100 prototype
The PaPeRo name was adopted in 2001

entries.name: Paro
entries.def: Therapeutic robot shaped like a baby harp seal, made to soothe and draw emotional responses from patients in hospitals and care homes, much like animal therapy.

entries.name: Pathfinder
entries.def: Retrofit autonomy kit that turns conventional orchard and vineyard tractors into driverless machines supervised from a control room by one operator running several tractors.
specs: Retrofit actuation of steering, throttle, brakes and implement controls on existing tractors
Lidar, radar, cameras and corrected satellite positioning
Driverless row work supervised from a control room and mobile app, one operator overseeing several tractors
facts: Works as a brand agnostic kit fitted to tractors from several manufacturers
Announced a collaboration with the farm equipment maker CNH on autonomous tractors
Bluewhite was acquired by the defence and technology group Elbit Systems

entries.name: PatrolBot
entries.def: Service robot made in the United States by ActivMedia Robotics, a company later renamed Mobile Robots Inc.

entries.name: Pave
entries.def: Robot that finds and seals cracks in asphalt for paving contractors.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Pave Robotics

entries.name: Peacock Clock
entries.def: Large eighteenth century automaton clock with three mechanical birds of full life size, created by the businessman James Cox.
facts: Entered Catherine the Great's collection in 1781 with help from Grigory Potemkin
Exhibited at the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg
Shown every day on a Russian television channel

entries.name: Peak Robotics KX-2
entries.def: Collaborative selective compliance assembly robot arm (SCARA) made by Peak Robotics for automating laboratory work in the life sciences.

entries.name: Pepper
entries.def: Wheeled social humanoid used for greeting and information duties in shops, banks and airports, with about 17,000 units sold before production ended.
specs: 20 electric servo joints on a three wheel omnidirectional base
Lasers, sonar, infrared, 3D depth camera, two 2D cameras, four microphone array, touch sensors
NAOqi framework with face and speech recognition and a chest tablet interface
facts: About 17,000 units sold across roughly 70 countries
Deployed in SoftBank Mobile stores, HSBC branches, Carrefour supermarkets and cruise ships
Production halted around 2021 and maker Aldebaran placed in receivership in June 2025

entries.name: Perceptive
entries.def: Robotic system that pairs a new dental imaging method with automated tooth cutting, such as preparing a tooth for a crown.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Perceptive Technologies

entries.name: Perseverance
entries.def: Mars 2020 rover exploring Jezero crater, caching rock cores for possible return to Earth and testing oxygen production from atmospheric carbon dioxide.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive with four corner steering
Mastcam-Z, SuperCam, PIXL, SHERLOC, RIMFAX radar, MEDA weather station
AutoNav and terrain relative navigation allowing driving while thinking
facts: First mission to cache rock cores on another planet
MOXIE made oxygen from Martian carbon dioxide
Deployed Ingenuity, the first powered aircraft to fly on another planet

entries.name: PETMAN
entries.def: An anthropomorphic test rig that marched in chemical suits to trial protective clothing.

entries.name: Philip K. Dick Android
entries.def: Humanlike android modeled on the science fiction author Philip K. Dick, built by Hanson Robotics in 2005 and able to converse using a model trained on his writings.
facts: First shown publicly at Wired NextFest in 2005

entries.name: Phobot
entries.def: Robot made from Lego by students at the University of Amsterdam that mimics being afraid and conquering fear step by step, intended to help children face phobias.
facts: Voted public favourite at a human robot interaction conference in Amsterdam

entries.name: Phoenix
entries.def: Hydraulically actuated general purpose humanoid built around highly dexterous hands, trialled in a Canadian retail store and with automotive supplier Magna.
specs: Miniaturised hydraulic actuators, particularly in the hands and wrists
Stereo vision with tactile sensing in the fingers
Carbon control system blending learned policies with teleoperation
facts: Completed a commercial pilot at a Canadian Tire store in Ontario in 2023
Automotive manufacturing partnership with Magna announced in March 2024
One of the few current humanoids using hydraulic rather than electric actuation

entries.name: Phony Pony
entries.def: Early electrically driven quadruped from USC, generally recognised as the first walking machine in the United States controlled entirely by a computer.
specs: Electric motors at the hip and knee of each leg
facts: Walked and trotted under computer control without human balance corrections

entries.name: Pickle

Head camera, IMU, servo position load and temperature feedback
Linux and ROS software stack published as an open platform
facts: Used by teams in RoboCup humanoid kid size soccer competition
Mechanical design and software released as an open platform
Successor to the widely used DARwIn-OP research biped

entries.name: Robotti
entries.def: Self propelled implement carrier that straddles crop beds and pulls seed drills, hoes and sprayers autonomously along pre planned tracks on European farms.
specs: Self propelled wheeled implement carrier straddling the bed, with three point hitch and power take off
Corrected satellite positioning with safety lidar and contact bumpers
Autonomous work along pre planned tracks with remote monitoring and stop on obstacle detection
facts: Sold commercially in Europe as a CE marked autonomous field machine
Used for seeding, mechanical weeding and precision spraying in vegetables and arable crops
Developed in Denmark out of research at Aarhus University

entries.name: RoboTuna
entries.def: Line of robotic fish that a team at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology built while investigating designs for autonomous underwater vehicles.

entries.name: RoboTurb
entries.def: Welding robot developed at the Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina in Brazil to repair turbine blades, built as a redundant robot mounted on a flexible rail.

refs.label: Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina website

entries.name: Roboty
entries.def: Self balancing differential wheeled robot with speech and object recognition, described as the first autonomous robot in Yemen and meant to be controlled mainly by voice.
facts: The project's eventual aim is a robot that can play chess

entries.name: RoboX
entries.def: Swiss mobile robot, 168 cm tall and 64 cm wide, that appeared at the Expo 02 exhibition in 2002.

entries.name: Roboy
entries.maker: University of Zurich Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
entries.def: Tendon driven humanoid built in about nine months by a Zurich led consortium to copy human muscle and tendon actuation in a child sized body.
specs: About 48 brushless motors driving tendons with force sensing
Cameras, microphone, tendon force and joint position sensing
Speech and face recognition driving scripted interaction
facts: Built in roughly nine months by a consortium of universities and companies
Tendon driven musculoskeletal design on a largely 3D printed skeleton

refs.label: University of Zurich Artificial Intelligence Laboratory website

entries.name: Robug III
entries.def: Mobile robot shaped like a spider, developed at the University of Portsmouth in the United Kingdom.

entries.name: Rocky 7
entries.def: JPL research microrover that added a camera mast and sampling arm to the Sojourner class design, field tested in the Mojave Desert.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive with two steered wheels
Deployable camera mast, stereo cameras, sampling arm and scoop
Waypoint driving with onboard hazard detection
facts: Prototyped mast based science operations later used on Mars
Used for remote science team field trials in the Mojave Desert

entries.name: Rodeo
entries.def: Robotic technician that performs oil changes at fleet depots.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Rodeo Robotics

entries.name: Roin
entries.def: Robots that finish commercial concrete floors, with one person supervising the work of several crews; the company was acquired.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Roin Technologies

entries.name: Rollin' Justin
entries.def: Wheeled humanoid from DLR with torque controlled arms and hands, commanded from the International Space Station in orbital telerobotics experiments.
specs: Torque controlled electric joints with tendon driven hands
Torque sensors in nearly all joints, two stereo cameras, five depth cameras, inertial units
facts: Commanded from the International Space Station in the METERON SUPVIS Justin experiments
Torque sensing in nearly every joint for compliant whole body control
Introduced in 2009
Developed at the DLR institute in Wessling, Germany
Operates wirelessly

entries.name: Roo ver
entries.def: Lunar rover funded by the Australian Space Agency and under construction by the ELO2 consortium, with launch to the Moon's south polar region planned for 2030.
facts: The first Australian lunar rover
Scheduled to fly on the Intuitive Machines Nova-D lander

entries.name: Roomba
entries.def: Disc shaped domestic vacuum robot that cleans floors on its own and returns to a dock, the product that created the home robot market.
specs: Two drive wheels with a caster, side brush and counter rotating brushes or rubber rollers
Rechargeable battery with a self charging home base
Bumper, cliff and dirt detection sensors, with an upward camera on later models
Random coverage on early models, visual mapping and systematic rows on later ones
facts: Launched in September 2002 and helped create the consumer robot market
IRobot filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in December 2025 and was acquired the following year
Amazon's proposed acquisition of iRobot was abandoned in 2024

entries.name: Roomba 980
entries.def: First Roomba to map rooms with a camera and connect to a phone app.

entries.name: Roomba j7
entries.def: Roomba model with a front camera that recognises cords, socks and pet waste and steers around them.

entries.name: Root
entries.def: Coding robot that drives on whiteboards, drawing and erasing as it runs a program, developed at Harvard's Wyss Institute and later sold by iRobot.

entries.name: Ropid
entries.def: Small humanoid robot created by Tomotaka Takahashi of Robo Garage at Kyoto University.
facts: Its name combines the words robot and rapid

entries.name: ROPOS
entries.def: Remotely operated underwater vehicle used mainly for science, built in Vancouver by International Submarine Engineering and later purchased by the Canadian federal government.
facts: The same government program also operated the crewed submersible Pisces IV

entries.name: ROSA
entries.def: Robotic surgical assistant first developed by Medtech in France for brain and spine procedures, later used for knee replacement.

entries.name: Rosalind Franklin
entries.maker: Airbus Defence and Space for the European Space Agency
entries.def: European ExoMars rover built to drill two metres below the surface of Oxia Planum in search of preserved organic biosignatures.
specs: Six wheel flexible chassis with wheel walking locomotion
Solar arrays with radioisotope heater units for night survival
PanCam, ISEM, CLUPI, WISDOM radar, Ma_MISS borehole spectrometer, MOMA, MicrOmega, Raman spectrometer
Onboard autonomous navigation for long single sol traverses
facts: Designed to drill two metres deep, far deeper than any previous Mars rover
Flight model is built and awaiting a 2028 launch
Named after the chemist whose X ray work underpinned DNA structure

refs.label: Airbus Defence and Space for the European Space Agency website

entries.name: Rosetta
entries.def: Robotic space probe which orbited comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko.

entries.name: ROV KIEL 6000
entries.def: Electrically powered remotely operated vehicle made by Schilling Robotics of California and owned by Germany's GEOMAR, used for scientific work down to 6,000 m.
facts: Linked to its ship by a deep sea glass fibre cable
Can work from ships of opportunity with enough deck space, power and crane capacity

entries.name: ROV Odysseus 6K
entries.def: Deep diving remotely operated vehicle from Pelagic Research Services of South Wellfleet, Massachusetts, rated to work as deep as 6,000 m of seawater.
facts: Maximum rated depth of 6,000 m (20,000 ft)
Name combines the hero Odysseus with its 6,000 m depth rating

entries.name: ROV PHOCA
entries.def: Compact remotely operated underwater vehicle built by Sub-Atlantic in Aberdeen and owned by the GEOMAR ocean research centre in Kiel, able to dive to 3000 m.
facts: A COMANCHE type ROV
Small enough to deploy from mid sized research ships
Designed for work class and intervention tasks

entries.name: ROV SuBastian
entries.def: Tethered remotely operated underwater vehicle that the Schmidt Ocean Institute deploys from its research ship RV Falkor (too) for deep sea science, capable of reaching 4,500 m.
facts: Rated to depths of 4,500 m
Capabilities include sample collection, seafloor mapping, photomosaicing and 4K video

entries.name: Rovio
entries.def: Wireless networked robot made by WowWee that carries a webcam, letting its user watch the camera feed and drive it remotely over the internet.
facts: Can be controlled from a PC, Mac, smartphone, PDA or PSP

entries.name: ROVVER X
entries.def: Six wheel drive tethered sewer inspection crawler with a pan and tilt camera, driven by a technician from a surface reel and controller.
specs: Six wheel drive crawler with interchangeable wheels and axles for different pipe diameters
Power and data supplied over the tether from a motorised surface reel
Pan, tilt and zoom camera with lighting, plus optional laser profiling and sonar modules
Remotely operated from a surface controller, with powered cable management
facts: Inspects pipe from small municipal laterals up to large diameter trunk mains
A satellite camera variant inspects lateral connections from inside the mainline
Widely used by North American municipal sewer departments and inspection contractors

entries.name: Roxo
entries.def: FedEx sidewalk delivery robot built on DEKA balancing wheel technology that could climb curbs and stairs, tested in several cities and cancelled in 2022.
specs: Powered wheel clusters derived from the DEKA iBot, able to balance and climb kerbs and stairs
Autonomous sidewalk navigation supervised by human minders during public trials
facts: Unveiled in February 2019 and developed with DEKA Development and Research, founded by Dean Kamen
Tested in Memphis, Tennessee, Plano, Texas, and Manchester, New Hampshire
FedEx shut the Roxo programme down in October 2022

entries.name: Roybi
entries.def: Companion robot that relies on artificial intelligence software, made by the company Roybi Robot.

entries.name: RP-VITA
entries.def: Hospital telemedicine robot on an autonomous wheeled base, letting a specialist examine patients remotely without a nurse steering the machine.
specs: Differential drive base derived from the iRobot Ava platform
Autonomous point to point navigation with mapping and collision avoidance
facts: Received United States regulatory clearance for hospital use in 2012
Built on the iRobot Ava mobile base
InTouch Health was acquired by Teladoc Health in 2020

entries.name: RS Media
entries.def: Biomorphic robot from WowWee built on the Robosapien V2 body, running Linux based software and able to record and replay sound, photos and video.
facts: Body is based on the Robosapien V2
Software is built on a Linux kernel
Uses a walking system designed by Mark Tilden

entries.name: RU-27
entries.def: Experimental American underwater glider run by ocean scientists at Rutgers University that in 2009 made the first robotic crossing of the Atlantic beneath the surface.
facts: Nicknamed Scarlet Knight, like the university's sports teams
A modified Slocum glider
The Atlantic crossing, finished in December 2009, took 221 days

entries.name: RuBot II
entries.def: Rubik's Cube solving robot built by Irish roboticist and inventor Pete Redmond that entered the Guinness Book of World Records as the fastest machine of its kind.
facts: Also known as the Cubinator

entries.name: RunBot
entries.def: Miniature two legged walking robot that uses reflexes triggered by foot contact sensors instead of a central pattern generator to produce its gait.
facts: Built in 2005 by Tao Geng as part of his PhD
Its walking speed can be improved through reinforcement learning
Its movement draws on the work of neurophysiologist Nikolai Bernstein

entries.name: RVR
entries.def: Programmable tracked robot from Sphero with a port for adding single board computers and sensors.

entries.name: s-bot
entries.def: Small differential wheeled mobile robot, 15 cm in size, developed at the EPFL in Lausanne between 2001 and 2004 for swarm robotics research in the Swarm bots project.
facts: Ranked 39th in Wired magazine's 2006 list of The 50 Best Robots Ever
Swarm bots was coordinated by Marco Dorigo
Built by engineers in Dario Floreano's group with help from student projects

entries.name: S-One
entries.def: The DRC Trials winner from a Google acquired startup later shut down; its walking was years ahead.

entries.name: S1
entries.def: A dual armed humanoid noted for startling manipulation speed in kitchen demonstrations.

entries.name: S8 MaxV Ultra
entries.def: The flagship of the robot vacuum arms race, with a self emptying, self washing dock.

entries.name: Sabor
entries.def: Humanoid robot built in Switzerland, with a body shaped broadly like that of a person.

entries.name: SAFFiR
entries.maker: Virginia Tech with the US Naval Research Laboratory
entries.def: Bipedal firefighting robot developed for the US Navy that walked a decommissioned ship's compartments and aimed a hose at a live fire.
specs: Linear series elastic actuators with titanium springs
Infrared stereo vision, rotating lidar, six axis force and torque sensors in the ankles
Semi autonomous task execution with a human supervisor in the loop
facts: Fought a live fire aboard the ex-USS Shadwell in November 2014
Funded by the Office of Naval Research with the Naval Research Laboratory

refs.label: Virginia Tech with the US Naval Research Laboratory website

entries.name: Saildrone Explorer
entries.def: Wind and solar powered uncrewed sailing vessel that gathers ocean and weather data on missions lasting months.
facts: A Saildrone completed the first autonomous circumnavigation of Antarctica in 2019

entries.name: Sally
entries.def: Vending machine sized robot that assembled salads and bowls from refrigerated canisters, bought by DoorDash in 2021.

entries.name: Salvius
entries.def: Open source humanoid made in the United States, favouring salvaged and recycled parts to cut costs, with the goal of working in an ordinary home.
facts: Built in 2008 and described as the first open source humanoid robot
Name derives from the word salvaged

entries.name: Sanbot
entries.def: Family of cloud connected service robots developed by Qihan Technology, a robotics and artificial intelligence firm based in Shenzhen, China.
facts: Released in three generations: Sanbot Elf, Sanbot King Kong and Sanbot Nano

entries.name: Sarcoman
entries.def: Show robot from Sarcos that performs either under the live control of a human operator or from programmed computer routines in automated shows.

entries.name: Sarcos-Raytheon XOS
entries.def: Powered exoskeleton developed by Sarcos in the United States, a wearable robotic frame that moves in step with the person inside it.

entries.name: Sawfish harvester
entries.def: Submersible logging robot made by Triton Logging that uses large pincers and a chainsaw to fell trees flooded by dams and float them to the surface.
facts: Targets forests flooded when dams are built nearby
Submerged wood stays usable for long periods

entries.name: Sawyer
entries.def: Single armed, seven axis collaborative robot from the makers of Baxter, with a screen that shows simple facial expressions.

entries.name: Scarab
entries.def: Lunar prospecting testbed rover with a body that kneels to press a drill into the ground, tested on Hawaiian volcanic soil.
specs: Four wheel drive on a body that kneels and changes its footprint
Battery electric drive designed for very low power operation
Laser scanner for driving in darkness, drill and volatiles payload
Teleoperated with autonomous navigation in darkness
facts: Kneels so its own weight provides drilling reaction force
Drilled with NASA's RESOLVE payload during Mauna Kea field tests

entries.name: Scarecrow
entries.def: Stripped down mobility twin of Curiosity built at reduced mass so its Earth weight matches the flight rover's weight on Mars.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive matching the flight rover
External umbilical or battery power during tests
Instrumented wheels with motion tracking during trials
facts: Mass tuned so Earth tests reproduce Martian wheel loading
Used to test escape routes from soft sand before commanding Curiosity

entries.name: SCITOS G5
entries.def: A German service robot base that has guided museum visitors for years.

entries.name: Scooba
entries.def: Floor washing robot from iRobot that sprayed, scrubbed and squeegeed hard floors.

entries.name: Scooptram ST18
entries.def: Articulated underground loader rated at eighteen tonnes that can be run remotely from surface or drive itself between loading and dumping points.
specs: Articulated four wheel drive underground loader with a front bucket
Diesel engine driving a hydrostatic or torque converter transmission
Onboard laser scanners for drift navigation with remote video for loading
Scooptram Automation allows autonomous tramming with remote operator loading from a surface station
facts: Used in underground metal mines worldwide on production and development work
Epiroc was spun out of Atlas Copco as a separate mining equipment company in 2018
Automation packages range from teleremote operation to fully autonomous tramming cycles

entries.name: Scout
entries.def: Robotic boat built by students from Tiverton, Rhode Island, in an attempt to become the first autonomous craft to cross the Atlantic Ocean.
facts: Project begun in 2010 by Dylan Rodriguez and Max Kramers
First crossing attempt launched from Sakonnet Point on 29 June 2013
Third attempt in August 2013 set a distance record for an unmanned Atlantic voyage

entries.name: Scout II
entries.def: Minimalist running quadruped from McGill with only one actuated joint per leg and passive springy lower legs.
specs: One electric motor per leg at the hip with passive compliant prismatic legs
facts: Bounded and climbed stairs using a single actuator per leg
Frequently cited as evidence that leg compliance can simplify running control

entries.name: Scribbler
entries.def: Small, inexpensive programmable educational robot from Parallax with several sensor systems, able to navigate on its own and respond to its surroundings.

entries.name: Scrubber 50
entries.def: Commercial scrubbing robot the size of a walk behind machine that cleans roughly 500 to 1,300 square metres an hour without a driver.
specs: 24 V 60 Ah lithium iron phosphate battery with a two hour charge
2D lidar, 3D depth camera, colour camera and collision sensors
Maps the site and repeats cleaning plans with obstacle avoidance
facts: Clean water tank holds 30 litres and the recovery tank 24 litres
Practical cleaning rate of about 500 to 1,300 square metres an hour
Gausium was founded in Shanghai in 2013

entries.name: Scythe M.52
entries.def: Commercial grade autonomous zero turn mower with a fifty two inch deck that mows areas an operator has driven around once.
specs: Electric all wheel drive with a 52 inch side discharge cutting deck
Battery electric, recharging in six to eight hours on a 240 volt supply
Eight high dynamic range cameras, twelve ultrasonic sensors, two inertial measurement units and satellite positioning
Operator teaches the mow zone perimeter once, then the mower works it autonomously
facts: Mows about 1.5 to 2 acres per hour with a cut height range of 1.5 to 6 inches
Offered to commercial landscape contractors on a pay per acre service model
Cuts fuel, noise and emissions compared with petrol zero turn mowers

entries.name: SDR-4X
entries.def: Humanoid robot developed in Japan by Sony; its SDR designation stands for Sony Dream Robot.

entries.name: SE01
entries.def: EngineAI's full size humanoid with a strikingly natural human gait.

entries.name: Sea Dragon class ROV
entries.def: Series of Chinese work class remotely operated vehicles for oil platform servicing, salvage and rescue, all derived from the original Sea Dragon.
facts: The original Sea Dragon could dive to 3,500 meters
Later models were adapted to different operating conditions

entries.name: SeaBotix ROV
entries.def: Series of underwater remotely operated vehicles marketed by Teledyne Marine under the SeaBotix brand name.

entries.name: Seaglider
entries.def: Long endurance underwater glider developed at the University of Washington that profiles ocean temperature and salinity for months at a time.

entries.name: SeaPerch
entries.def: Educational kit and curriculum in which school students build a basic remotely operated underwater vehicle from PVC pipe and other everyday materials.
facts: Launched in 2003 by the MIT Sea Grant College Program
Inspired by the 1997 book Build Your Own Underwater Robot and other Wet Projects
Backed by the Office of Naval Research to develop future naval engineers

entries.name: Seekur
entries.def: An all weather omnidirectional research truck of the pre-AMR era.

entries.name: Senhance
entries.def: Laparoscopic surgical robot with eye tracking camera control and haptic feedback for the surgeon.

entries.name: Sensei X
entries.def: Medical robot that helps physicians guide a catheter, a small flexible tube, during complex minimally invasive operations.
facts: Guides catheters used to treat target tissue and deliver medicines

entries.name: Senster
entries.def: Robotic artwork by Edward Ihnatowicz that Philips commissioned for the Evoluon in Eindhoven, the Netherlands, where it was exhibited from 1970 until its dismantling in 1974.
facts: Dismantled in 1974; a restoration followed in the late 2010s

entries.name: Sentry
entries.def: Autonomous underwater vehicle made by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution that carries instruments for collecting samples, images and readings in the deep sea.
facts: Designed to dive to 6,000 metres (20,000 ft)

entries.name: SEROPI
entries.def: Humanoid robot that moves on a wheeled base rather than legs, developed by KITECH.

entries.name: Serve Gen3
entries.def: Third generation four wheeled sidewalk delivery robot that carries restaurant orders on United States city sidewalks under Level 4 autonomy with remote assistance.
specs: Four wheeled electric drive with a lockable insulated cargo bin
Rechargeable battery, with roughly twice the range of the previous generation
Ouster REV7 digital lidar, camera suite and an NVIDIA Jetson Orin compute module
Level 4 sidewalk autonomy with remote human assistance on request
facts: Cargo bin holds four sixteen inch pizzas, about fifteen percent more volume than the prior generation
Serve deployed its 1,000th robot and has since reported 2,000 robots operating on the Uber Eats platform
Grew out of the Postmates X robotics group before becoming an independent public company

entries.name: Servi
entries.def: Tray carrying restaurant robot that brings food from the kitchen to tables and returns dirty dishes along a mapped route.
specs: Rechargeable battery with a charging dock
Lidar and depth cameras with near zero blind spot coverage
Self driving navigation on a learned floor map with obstacle avoidance
facts: Distributed in Japan by SoftBank Robotics from 2020
LG Electronics became the majority owner of Bear Robotics in 2024
Carries about 10 kg per tray, roughly 30 kg in total

entries.name: Servo7
entries.def: Robot that unloads loose cartons from shipping containers, used by logistics firms including DHL and PostNL.

entries.name: Sewbo
entries.def: Industrial robot that carries out sewing work, invented by the American company Sewbo, Inc.
facts: Its maker is headquartered in Seattle, Washington

entries.name: Shadow Dexterous Hand
entries.def: Dexterous robot hand from the Shadow Robot Company in London, built to human hand size and shape with the same full set of degrees of freedom.
facts: Sold in pneumatic and electric versions
Used by NASA, Bielefeld University and Carnegie Mellon University
Used in EU research projects including HANDLE

entries.name: Shakey
entries.def: The first mobile robot able to reason about its own actions, a wheeled machine that pushed blocks around laboratory rooms under program control.
specs: Wheeled cart with a drive base and a camera mast
Onboard batteries with a radio link to a mainframe computer
Television camera, sonar range finders and bump detectors
Off board planning with the STRIPS planner over a radio link
facts: Work on Shakey produced the A star search algorithm and the Hough transform
Inducted into the Robot Hall of Fame in 2004 and marked with an IEEE Milestone
On display at the Computer History Museum in Mountain View, California

entries.name: Shalu
entries.def: Humanoid robot for social interaction and teaching that Mumbai computer science teacher Dinesh Kunwar Patel built out of discarded materials.

entries.name: SherpaTT
entries.def: Hybrid wheeled leg rover with actively articulated suspension, field tested in the Utah desert and in Morocco for Mars analogue work.
specs: Four legs with driven and steered wheels and active ground adaption
Lithium polymer battery packs with autonomous switching
Rotating lidar, laser rangefinder, high resolution camera, wheel force torque sensors
Autonomous navigation with active suspension control
facts: Active suspension keeps the body level on rough slopes
Completed multi week Mars analogue field campaigns in Utah and Morocco

entries.name: Shinkei
entries.def: Robot for fishing boats that uses computer vision to apply the Japanese ikejime method, which keeps fish fresher for longer.
