refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Shinkei Systems

entries.name: SICO
entries.def: Entertainment robot made by International Robotics and offered commercially, featured in the film Rocky IV.

entries.name: Silver Arm
entries.def: Early robot arm built by David Silver at MIT that used touch and pressure sensors to assemble small parts.

entries.name: Silver Swan
entries.def: Clockwork swan automaton made by James Cox in the 18th century, now displayed at the Bowes Museum in Barnard Castle, County Durham.
facts: Dates from 1773
Bought by museum founder John Bowes from a Paris jeweller in 1872

entries.name: Sina Robotic Surgical System
entries.def: Surgical robot for minimally invasive procedures made by Sina Robotics and Medical Innovators, used for prostatectomies and a growing range of other operations.
facts: Growing use in heart valve repair
Also applied to renal and gynaecological procedures

entries.name: SJT class ROUV
entries.maker: Shenyang Institute of Automation and Shanghai Jiao Tong University
entries.def: Chinese family of remotely operated underwater vehicles created as a joint project of the Shenyang Institute of Automation and the underwater engineering institute of Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
facts: General designer was Zhu Jimao, a Shanghai Jiao Tong University professor
Zhu Jimao also designed the earlier Type 7103 DSRV
Experience from the series fed into many later Chinese ROUVs

entries.name: SkyFood
entries.def: Autonomous delivery robot from the Brazilian robotics company TracFtech that doubles as a mobile digital advertising display.

entries.name: Skypod
entries.def: Warehouse robot that drives across the floor and then climbs the face of the racking to retrieve bins stored up to 14 metres high.
specs: Four wheel drive chassis that grips rack rails and climbs vertically
Onboard navigation coordinated by Exotec fleet software
facts: Climbs racking to about 14 m to reach stored bins
Named customers include Carrefour, Decathlon and Gap
Throughput is scaled by adding robots to an existing rack

entries.name: Slicer
entries.def: Remote controlled combat robot that competed in the Dutch version of Robot Wars, the television series in which teams fight their machines in an arena.

entries.name: Slocum glider
entries.def: Buoyancy driven underwater glider that travels for weeks by changing its displacement, named after the sailor Joshua Slocum.
facts: A Slocum glider named Scarlet Knight crossed the Atlantic in 2009

entries.name: SOFIE
entries.def: Surgical robot developed at Eindhoven University of Technology as part of Linda van den Bedem's doctoral thesis, the first such robot to give the surgeon force feedback.
facts: Name stands for Surgeon's Operating Force feedback Interface Eindhoven

entries.name: Sojourner
entries.def: Six wheeled microrover of the Mars Pathfinder mission, the first wheeled vehicle to drive on another planet, operating in Ares Vallis.
specs: Six independently driven wheels on a rocker bogie chassis
Solar array with non rechargeable lithium thionyl chloride batteries
Three cameras, laser stripe hazard detection, alpha proton X ray spectrometer
Operator designated waypoints with onboard hazard detection
facts: First wheeled robot to drive on another planet
Operated 83 sols against a planned seven sol mission
Returned 550 images and 16 rock and soil chemistry measurements

entries.name: Solix
entries.def: Solar powered four wheeled scouting and spraying robot that inspects individual plants and applies herbicide only where weeds are found in row crops.
specs: Four wheeled lightweight electric drive with a boom mounted sensing and spray head
Onboard solar panels charging a battery pack
Cameras with edge processing for plant level weed, pest and disease detection
Autonomous field scouting and targeted spraying coordinated by the company's ALICE decision platform
facts: Developed in Brazil and field tested with United States land grant universities including Purdue
The Solix Sprayer variant reached commercial availability
Designed to run around the clock on solar charge with self refilling spray logistics

entries.name: Solo 12
entries.def: Open hardware torque controlled quadruped weighing a few kilograms, designed so any laboratory could build one from printed parts.
specs: Twelve back drivable brushless actuators with low gear ratios
Off board torque control over a low latency link
facts: Complete hardware design released as open source so laboratories can build their own
Developed jointly by the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, New York University and LAAS-CNRS

entries.name: Solo 8
entries.def: A fully open hardware research quadruped reproducible on a lab budget.

entries.name: Somatic
entries.def: Mobile robot that cleans restrooms in office buildings on its own.

entries.name: Somnox Sleep Robot
entries.def: Capsule shaped robot that rises and falls in a fixed breathing rhythm, meant to help users fall asleep by matching their own breathing to it.
facts: Its maker claims users fall asleep by subconsciously matching its breathing

entries.name: Sophia
entries.def: Expressive interaction humanoid known for public appearances and media work, produced in small numbers and supplied to research, education and events.
specs: Roughly 60 electric actuators driving a face cast in a patented elastomer skin
Mains or onboard battery depending on configuration
Cameras in the eyes, microphones, chest depth sensing
Mixture of scripted content, chatbot dialogue and human operator control
facts: Granted honorary Saudi citizenship in 2017 during a Riyadh conference appearance
Appeared at United Nations events and in numerous televised interviews
Sold alongside the smaller desktop Little Sophia education robot

entries.name: SORA-Q
entries.maker: JAXA with Tomy, Sony and Doshisha University
entries.def: Transformable ball shaped lunar robot the size of a baseball that photographed the tipped over SLIM lander in January 2024.
specs: Two hemispherical shell wheels with a stabilising tail and two crawling gaits
Autonomous imaging sequence after release with no live control
facts: Among the smallest and lightest rovers ever landed on the Moon
Took the image showing SLIM resting nose down
Data relayed to Earth by the companion LEV-1 hopper

refs.label: JAXA with Tomy, Sony and Doshisha University website

entries.name: SORA-Q Flagship Model
entries.def: Radio controlled mobile toy robot released in 2023 by the Japanese toy company Tomy as the flagship model bearing the SORA-Q name.

entries.name: Sorato
entries.def: Four kilogram carbon fibre rover built for the Google Lunar XPRIZE by Team Hakuto, completed and tested but never launched.
specs: Four wheel drive with independent motors
facts: Flight model completed for the Google Lunar XPRIZE but never flew
The team behind it became the lunar company ispace

entries.name: Space Exploration Vehicle
entries.def: NASA pressurised rover prototype on a twelve wheel chassis, tested in Arizona desert campaigns as a mobile habitat for two crew.
specs: Twelve wheels in six pivoting pairs allowing omnidirectional driving
Crew driven with a remote teleoperation capability
facts: Wheel pairs pivot through a full circle for sideways driving
Crews lived aboard during two week desert field tests

refs.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration website

entries.name: SpaceBok
entries.def: Jumping quadruped built by Swiss students to study legged movement in low gravity for lunar and asteroid exploration.
specs: Electric motors with spring energy storage in each leg
facts: Tested in simulated lunar and microgravity conditions at the European Space Agency's ESTEC laboratory
Used a reaction wheel to control body orientation during long jumps

refs.label: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab website

entries.name: Sparko
entries.def: The world's fair robot dog who barked, begged and sat beside Elektro.

entries.name: Sparrow
entries.def: Robot arm from Amazon that uses computer vision and suction to pick individual products from bins in fulfilment centres.

entries.name: SPHERES
aka: Synchronized Position Hold Engage and Reorient Experimental Satellite
entries.def: Set of free flying robots developed by MIT's Space Systems Laboratory for NASA and the US military to test formation flight, docking and autonomy algorithms aboard the International Space Station.
facts: Each unit measures 22.9 by 21.3 by 21.3 cm, with a mass of 3.55 kg
Used as a low risk, expandable test bed for distributed spacecraft technology
Name stands for Synchronized Position Hold Engage and Reorient Experimental Satellite

entries.name: Sphero
entries.def: A programmable rolling ball that carried coding lessons into a million classrooms.

entries.name: Spirit
entries.def: Solar powered Mars Exploration Rover that worked in Gusev crater for six years and found mineral evidence of ancient hot water.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive with four corner steering
Solar arrays with rechargeable lithium ion batteries
Panoramic and navigation cameras, microscopic imager, alpha particle X ray and Moessbauer spectrometers, thermal emission spectrometer
Ground planned drives with onboard hazard avoidance and visual odometry
facts: Operated 2,208 sols against a planned 90 sol mission
Found silica rich deposits indicating an ancient hydrothermal setting
Drove 7.73 km before becoming stuck in soft sand

entries.name: Spirit 40
entries.def: Small electric quadruped from Ghost Robotics sold for research, swarm experiments and reconnaissance in confined spaces.
specs: Direct drive electric joint modules, three per leg
Proprioceptive blind walking with operator control and a developer interface
facts: Sized for stairwells and confined spaces where larger quadrupeds cannot work
Used for swarm and control research alongside the larger Vision 60

entries.name: Spot
entries.def: Electric inspection quadruped, the machine that turned legged robots into an off the shelf industrial product.
specs: Electric geared joint actuators, three per leg
Five stereo camera pairs, inertial measurement unit, optional lidar and thermal payloads
Autonomous route repetition with docking and remote operation
facts: Offered for general sale in June 2020 at 74,500 US dollars
Used for autonomous inspection on offshore platforms and in power stations, and for radiation surveys at Chernobyl in 2020
Hyundai Motor Group took a controlling stake in Boston Dynamics in 2021

entries.name: Spot Classic
entries.def: The hydraulic middleweight between BigDog and today's Spot.

entries.name: Spring Flamingo
entries.def: Planar walking biped at MIT that pioneered series elastic actuators and force controlled walking on flat ground and shallow slopes.
specs: Series elastic actuators with cable drives from body mounted motors
Intuitive force based walking control, boom constrained to the sagittal plane
facts: Early demonstration of series elastic actuation for legged robots
Control approach carried forward into later IHMC humanoid work

entries.name: Sprout
entries.def: A compact home humanoid from CTRL-labs and DeepMind alumni; acquired by Amazon in 2026.

entries.name: SPURV
entries.maker: University of Washington Applied Physics Laboratory
entries.def: Autonomous underwater research vehicle that the University of Washington's Applied Physics Laboratory built in 1957, becoming the US Navy's first AUV.
facts: Development was funded by the US Office of Naval Research
The navy used seven SPURVs until 1979

entries.name: Spyce
entries.def: Boston restaurant whose automated woks cooked grain bowls, founded by MIT graduates and bought by Sweetgreen in 2021.

entries.name: Spykee
entries.def: Toy robot from Meccano carrying a webcam, microphone and speaker that its owner can drive around the home from a computer, whether nearby or remotely through the internet.
facts: Can take photos and video and play sounds through its speaker
Connects to the internet over WiFi
Electronics built by the French startup WaveStorm

entries.name: Squawkers McCaw
entries.def: Animatronic toy parrot from the Fur Real range, modelled on a blue and yellow macaw and made to behave like a real parrot.

entries.name: Squirrel Robot
entries.def: Inspection robot built in France in 1990 by LIST to get into hazardous parts of nuclear plants and send back reports on conditions there.

entries.name: StackChan
aka: M5StackChan, Stack-chan, スタックチャン, K151
entries.def: Open source desktop robot sold as a product by the Chinese company M5Stack, with a mass of 187 g.

entries.name: Stanford arm
entries.def: Early robot arm offering six degrees of freedom, created by Victor Scheinman at Stanford University in 1969 and often used as a teaching example in robotics.
facts: Kinematic chain of two revolute base joints, one prismatic joint and one spherical joint

entries.name: Stanford Cart
entries.def: A camera cart that crossed a chair filled room in five hours, founding visual navigation.

entries.name: Stanford Doggo
entries.def: Open source quasi direct drive quadruped built by students for a few thousand dollars that set a vertical jumping record.
specs: Eight quasi direct drive brushless motors, two per leg
Inertial measurement unit, motor position sensing
Open loop gait state machine on a microcontroller
facts: Highest vertical jumping agility recorded for a legged robot when published in 2019
Complete mechanical and electrical design released as open source

entries.name: Stanford Pupper
entries.def: Open source servo driven quadruped derived from Stanford Doggo and designed as a teaching kit for legged robotics courses.
specs: Hobby scale servo actuators, three per leg
Python gait controller on a Raspberry Pi with game controller input
facts: Designed as a low cost teaching kit and used in university legged robotics courses
Design and software published openly, spawning many derivative kits

entries.name: Star1
entries.def: A sprinting humanoid clocked at record speed across the Gobi desert in trainers.

refs.label: Live Science, STAR1 in the Gobi Desert

entries.name: StarlETH
entries.def: Series elastic electric quadruped from ETH Zurich that showed compliant actuation could give small legged robots dynamic gaits.
specs: Series elastic electric actuators, three joints per leg
Joint encoders, spring deflection sensing, inertial measurement unit
Onboard virtual model and torque control
facts: Demonstrated torque controllable series elastic legs on a fully battery powered quadruped
Led directly to ANYmal and the ETH Zurich spin off ANYbotics

entries.name: Starship delivery robot
entries.def: Six wheeled sidewalk robot that carries groceries and meals a few kilometres from a hub to a customer, navigating autonomously with remote human oversight.
specs: Six wheels driven by electric hub motors
Cameras, ultrasonic sensors, radar, satellite positioning and inertial measurement
Autonomous navigation with remote operators supervising and able to take control
facts: Passed 9 million autonomous deliveries in October 2025, with a fleet of roughly 2,700 robots
Founded in 2014 in Tallinn, Estonia, by Skype co founders Ahti Heinla and Janus Friis
Delivers for Grubhub on university campuses, and for Co op and Tesco stores in the United Kingdom

entries.name: Stiquito
entries.def: Small, low cost six legged walking robot used since 1992 by universities, high schools and hobbyists.

entries.name: Stompy
entries.def: An open source humanoid released with plans and firmware for anyone to build.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, K-Scale Labs

entries.name: STR-1
entries.def: Radio controlled clearing robot derived from Lunokhod chassis work, used on the reactor building roofs at Chernobyl in 1986.
specs: Wheeled chassis derived from the Lunokhod self propelled chassis with a bulldozer blade
Silver zinc batteries giving several hours of work per charge
Mast mounted television cameras providing the operator's view
Radio teleoperation from a shielded control point
facts: Cleared about 90 tonnes of radioactive debris from Chernobyl roofs
Worked from 8 August to 10 October 1986 where people could not go

entries.name: Stretch
entries.def: A box moving mobile arm unloading trucks one carton per second at DHL.

entries.name: Stuntronics
entries.def: Untethered acrobatic figure that performs flips and poses in mid air after being launched from a swing.

entries.name: Submerged Dragon 1
entries.def: Chinese autonomous underwater vehicle, an uncrewed craft that operates beneath the sea surface under its own onboard control.

entries.name: SUMMIT-XL
entries.def: A Spanish research AMR base common in European labs and EU projects.

entries.name: Surena IV
entries.maker: University of Tehran, Center of Advanced Systems and Technologies
entries.def: Iranian full size humanoid with 43 degrees of freedom built to a low cost design that replaces force sensors with predictive foot contact sensing.
specs: Brushless direct current motors with harmonic drive gears
Predictive foot contact encoders, cameras, inertial unit
Onboard walking control with vision based manipulation
facts: Fourth generation of the Iranian Surena programme, which began in 2008
Uses low cost predictive foot sensors in place of six axis force sensors
The IEEE included it among the world's notable robots after assessing its performance

refs.label: University of Tehran, Center of Advanced Systems and Technologies website

entries.name: SwarmBot
entries.def: Lightweight autonomous farm platform that carries third party implements for spraying, mowing and seeding, with several machines working one paddock together.
specs: Lightweight self propelled wheeled platform carrying third party implements
Corrected satellite positioning, lidar and radar for obstacle detection
Autonomous paddock coverage with remote monitoring, designed so several robots work as a swarm
facts: Raised 30 million Australian dollars in 2025 to scale the fleet and expand into North America
Manufactured at a purpose built hub on Queensland's Darling Downs
Founded by Queensland grain farmers who wanted lighter machines than conventional tractors

entries.name: SwiftBot
entries.def: A premium server robot that reads gestures and dodges crowds.

entries.name: SWIFTI
entries.def: Small, fast arm from ABB that slows or stops when a person comes near, bridging industrial and collaborative robots.
facts: Model number CRB 1100

entries.name: Synphony
entries.def: Strawberry harvesting robot for California farms, paired with field analytics.

entries.name: T-52 Enryu
entries.def: Rescue robot produced by the Japanese robotics company Tmsuk for use in rescue work.

entries.name: T-HR3
entries.def: A teleoperated avatar humanoid that mirrors its pilot through force feedback exoskeleton controls.

entries.name: T3
entries.def: Hydraulic industrial robot from Cincinnati Milacron, the first commercially available industrial robot controlled by a minicomputer.
facts: Name stands for The Tomorrow Tool

entries.name: T7AMR
entries.def: Robotic ride on floor scrubber for retail and industrial floors that staff can drive manually or leave to clean a taught route alone.
specs: Ride on scrubber deck with squeegee and recovery tank
Teach and repeat route learning with obstacle avoidance from Brain Corp software
facts: Runs the Brain Corp autonomy platform used by several commercial scrubbers
Can be operated manually as a conventional ride on scrubber
Tennant later added the larger T16AMR for industrial sites

entries.name: Tally
entries.def: Slim retail robot that patrols store aisles photographing shelves to find out of stock items, misplaced products and wrong price labels.
specs: Slim wheeled base with a vertical camera tower and turn in place steering
Rechargeable battery with a base station
More than a dozen high resolution cameras with depth sensing and optional radio frequency identification
Map based aisle navigation with path planning and obstacle avoidance among shoppers
facts: Reads roughly 15,000 to 30,000 shelf barcodes an hour
Schnucks Markets became the first retail customer in 2017
In use in about 1,000 stores including BJ's Wholesale Club locations

entries.name: TALOS
entries.def: Torque controlled full size humanoid sold by PAL Robotics as a platform for whole body control and dynamic locomotion research in industry and academia.
specs: 32 high torque brushless DC motors with torque sensing in every joint
Joint torque sensors, IMU, RGB-D head camera, expandable sensor modules
ROS based whole body control stack supplied with the robot
facts: Torque sensing in every joint enables compliant whole body control
Sold commercially to industrial and academic robotics laboratories
Supplied with a ROS software stack and modular sensor expansion

entries.name: Taobotics
entries.def: Autonomous robots for retail stores from a company based in Shenzhen.

entries.name: Taurob Inspector
entries.def: Mobile robot certified under ATEX rules, made by the Austrian firm Taurob for offshore oil and gas sites and derived from its Taurob Tracker.
facts: Holds ATEX certification
Grew out of the Taurob Tracker during the OGRIP project

entries.name: Taurob Tracker
entries.def: Austrian remote controlled ground robot made by Taurob, first developed for fire brigade reconnaissance and now also used by armed forces, universities and oil and gas companies.
facts: Also used by civil defence units

entries.name: teaBOT
entries.def: Robotic kiosk that blends and brews loose leaf tea to order, placed in offices and showrooms as a workplace amenity.

entries.name: TekBots
entries.def: Programmable teaching robots that a number of universities use to give students a grounding in the basics of computer and electrical engineering.
facts: Used in teaching at several universities

entries.name: Tekken-II
entries.def: Small electric quadruped used to test neural oscillator gait control with reflexes on irregular outdoor ground.
specs: DC motors with gear reduction at each leg joint
Rate gyroscopes, inclinometers and foot contact switches
Central pattern generator with contact and attitude reflexes
facts: Widely cited demonstration of central pattern generator control on rough outdoor terrain
Part of the Patrush and Tekken family of quadrupeds from Kimura's laboratory

entries.name: Tekno the Robotic Puppy
entries.def: Electronic robot dog toy launched in late 2000 that became a worldwide hit, with sales passing 40 million in its first four years.
facts: Launched in late 2000
Sold more than 7 million units in its first season
Featured on the cover of Time magazine

entries.name: Telenoid
entries.def: A minimal, ghost like telepresence android reduced to the essence of a person.
facts: Released in August 2010
About 80 cm tall and weighs 5 kg
Body made of silicone rubber

entries.name: Teleo
entries.def: Retrofit that turns dozers, trucks and loaders into supervised autonomous machines so one operator can run several from a control room; the company was acquired.

entries.name: temi
entries.def: A telepresence and assistant robot that follows its owner from room to room.

entries.name: Tenacious
entries.def: Five kilogram European built micro rover with a scoop and an artwork payload, lost when the Resilience lander crashed in June 2025.
specs: Four wheel drive with a fixed regolith scoop
High definition forward camera and navigation cameras
Teleoperated from a European control centre
facts: First lunar rover built in Europe
Carried a contracted regolith sample purchase for NASA
Lost in the ispace Mission 2 landing failure

entries.name: Tennibot Rover
entries.def: Autonomous robot from the company Tennibot that gathers balls by itself, removing the need for a person to collect them.

entries.name: TEO
entries.maker: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, RoboticsLab
entries.def: Full size Spanish research humanoid used to study household tasks such as ironing, folding laundry and opening doors.
specs: Electric motors with harmonic drive gears
Monocular camera, RGB-D sensor, six axis force torque sensors at wrists and ankles
Distributed control across three onboard computers on the YARP middleware
facts: Demonstrated ironing and laundry folding as household task research
Successor to the RH-1 humanoid at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid

refs.label: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, RoboticsLab website

entries.name: TERMES
entries.def: Team of termite inspired autonomous robots from Harvard University that build structures from blocks by following simple rules, with no central controller, first shown in 2014.
facts: Prototype team demonstrated by Harvard researchers in 2014
Developed over four years
Coordinate through stigmergy rather than constant human supervision

entries.name: Tertill
entries.def: A solar garden weeding puck from a Roomba co inventor.

entries.name: The Grand Elephant
entries.def: Giant animatronic elephant built by the French theater company La Machine, about 12 m tall and 8 m wide, with a top speed of 1 km/h.

entries.name: The Trons
entries.def: Robot band of four machines that play music by themselves, built from spare parts and electronics by Hamilton based musician Greg Locke.
facts: Based in Hamilton, New Zealand
Made up of four robots built from scratch
Named after Hamilton's nickname, "The Tron"

entries.name: Theseus
entries.def: Magnetic robotic mouse built at Bell Labs in the United States in 1950.

entries.name: Thorvald
entries.def: Modular battery electric field platform best known for carrying ultraviolet lamps that kill mildew on strawberries and grapes during night passes.
specs: Modular four wheel drive electric platform with reconfigurable track width and clearance
Autonomous row navigation with remote monitoring, working unattended at night
facts: Ultraviolet C treatment module suppresses powdery mildew on strawberries and grapes without fungicide
Originated in research at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences
Offered as a service on commercial berry and vineyard operations in Europe and the United States

entries.name: Three finger prehensile robot
entries.def: Gripping unit with three fingers, dating from 1990, designed to fit the end of assembly robots in the car industry and lent by the Laboratoire de robotique de Paris.

entries.name: Thymio
entries.def: A friendly white classroom robot teaching programming to children across Europe.

refs.label: École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne website

entries.name: TIAGo
entries.def: Wheeled robot with a lifting torso and one arm from PAL Robotics, widely used as a research platform for home and care tasks.

entries.name: Tiangong
entries.def: Full size electrically driven humanoid from a Beijing state backed innovation centre, demonstrated running at about 6 km/h in April 2024.
specs: Multiple visual perception sensors with inertial measurement
Learned locomotion controller running on onboard computing
facts: Demonstrated a running gait at about 6 km/h on electric drives alone
Platform partly opened for outside developers

entries.name: Tico
entries.def: Spanish social robot made by Adele Robots to engage with people, chiefly at marketing events and in schools as a teacher's assistant.
facts: Works mainly at promotional events and in classrooms alongside teachers

entries.name: TiLR
entries.def: Telepresence robot from RoboDynamics Corporation that stands in for a remote user at another location, reducing the need for business travel.
facts: Described as the first enterprise grade telepresence robot

entries.name: TinyLineMarker Pro
entries.def: Battery electric marking robot that sprays sports field lines and construction layout marks to satellite coordinates loaded from a drawing.
specs: Battery electric wheeled robot with a paint spray marking head
Corrected satellite positioning with centimetre level accuracy
Marks loaded geometry autonomously while the operator monitors from a tablet
facts: Marks football, rugby and athletics geometry from stored templates in minutes
Also used to set out construction and utility layouts directly from drawings
Sold to sports clubs, municipalities and contractors across Europe and North America

entries.name: Tipu's Tiger
entries.def: Eighteenth century wooden automaton made for Tipu Sultan of Mysore, depicting a tiger attacking a British man, with a pipe organ inside its body.
facts: Internal mechanisms move one of the man's hands and make him wail while the tiger grunts
A side flap drops open to expose the keyboard of an 18 note organ
Measures 61 cm wide

entries.name: TITAN VIII
entries.def: Compact wire driven quadruped from the Hirose laboratory, built as a general purpose walking platform for research and teaching.
specs: DC motors in the body driving leg joints through wires and pulleys
External computer running statically stable crawl gaits
facts: Wire driven legs kept moving mass low, a design copied in later walking machines
One of the most cited members of the TITAN series of quadrupeds

entries.name: TITAN XI
entries.def: Seven tonne hydraulic quadruped built to drill anchor holes on steep slopes, among the largest walking machines ever completed.
specs: Hydraulic cylinders, three joints per leg
Operator controlled with computer assisted gait and posture
facts: One of the heaviest walking robots ever built at about seven tonnes
Used tethered winches for stability while drilling on slopes of up to thirty degrees

entries.name: Tlaloc II-TC
entries.def: Robot built to explore the tunnel found in 2003 beneath the Temple of the Feathered Serpent at Teotihuacan, the ancient site in central Mexico.
facts: Also known as the Tlaloc II Robot
Used at Teotihuacan, a site founded in the second century BC

entries.name: TM5
entries.def: Collaborative arm from Techman Robot with a camera built into the wrist for locating parts.

entries.name: Tobor
entries.def: Toy robot made in 1978 by Schaper Toys that responded to loud sounds or to a control box through the company's telesonic remote system.
facts: Stood about nine inches high
Among the first toys with an inexpensive remote control
Released to cash in on the science fiction craze

entries.name: TOPIO
entries.def: Two legged humanoid robot from the Vietnamese firm TOSY, built to compete against people at table tennis.
facts: In development at TOSY since 2005
Demonstrated at the International Robot Exhibition in Tokyo on 28 November 2007
TOPIO 3.0 stands roughly 1.88 m high with a mass of 120 kg

entries.name: TOPIO Dio
entries.def: Wheeled humanoid service robot made by the Vietnamese company Tosy to serve customers in restaurants and coffee shops or to mix cocktails.
facts: Moves on a three wheeled platform and has 28 degrees of freedom
Stands 125 cm tall and weighs 45 kg
Operated remotely using a built in camera and obstacle detector

entries.name: Topo
entries.def: Series of personal robots produced by Androbot in the 1980s for homes and schools, programmed wirelessly from an Apple II computer.
facts: Programmed in TopoBASIC, an adapted form of BASIC
Had no sensors and could not send information back to the computer

entries.name: TORO
entries.def: Torque controlled humanoid from DLR assembled from lightweight robot arm joint modules to test compliant whole body balancing and walking.
specs: Torque controlled electric drives with harmonic gears and joint torque sensors
Joint torque and position sensing, six axis foot force torque sensors, torso inertial unit, stereo camera head
facts: Assembled from DLR lightweight robot arm joint modules
Used to demonstrate multi contact whole body balancing

entries.name: Torobo
entries.def: A research grade torque controlled humanoid sold to manipulation labs.

entries.name: Toyota Partner Robot
entries.def: Series of humanoid robots from Toyota that debuted by playing drums and trumpets at Expo 2005 in Aichi, Japan.
facts: Five models: Versions 1 to 4 and the i-Foot
A 2009 video showed one running at 7 km/h on flat ground
Third generation humanoid T-HR3 followed in 2017

entries.name: Tradinno
entries.def: Huge animatronic dragon that walks and breathes fire, built to play the dragon in the Drachenstich play in Furth im Wald, Germany.
facts: Listed in the 2014 Guinness World Records as the largest walking robot
Name combines the words tradition and innovation

entries.name: Transcriptic
entries.def: Remote controlled robotic laboratory where researchers ran life science experiments over the internet.

entries.name: Treads Robot
entries.def: Educational robot from the American company True Robotics, intended for classroom use from kindergarten through grade 3.

entries.name: Trexo
entries.def: Powered walking exoskeleton that lets children with conditions such as cerebral palsy take steps, often for the first time.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Trexo Robotics

entries.name: Trilobite
entries.def: The first mass market robot vacuum cleaner, a disc shaped machine that sensed rooms with ultrasound and returned to its dock to recharge.
specs: Two drive wheels with casters and a removable roller brush
Rechargeable battery with a docking station
Ultrasonic transducers, with infrared cliff sensors on the version 2.0
Ultrasonic ranging with wall following and automatic return to the charging dock
facts: Demonstrated as a prototype on BBC Tomorrow's World in 1996
Reached the market in 2001, before the first Roomba
A version 2.0 followed in 2004 before the line was dropped

entries.name: TRON 1
entries.def: A multi modal point foot biped platform for locomotion research.

entries.name: Troody
entries.def: Experimental robot from the United States, dating from 1995, that was designed to imitate a dinosaur.

entries.name: Tuesday
entries.def: Home robot from a New York startup built to pick up and tidy rooms.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Tuesday Labs

entries.name: TUG T3
entries.def: Hospital courier robot that tows carts of medication, meals, linen and waste, calling elevators and automatic doors over the building network.
specs: Rechargeable battery with an autonomous charging dock
Laser scanners, sonar and infrared sensors with contact bumpers
Laser and inertial SLAM on a stored map, integrated with elevators and doors
facts: Deployed at hospitals including UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay
Tows loaded carts of up to about 453 kg
Aethon was acquired by ST Engineering in 2019

entries.name: TurtleBot
entries.def: Personal robot kit that runs open source software, first developed at Willow Garage in November 2010 by Melonee Wise and Tully Foote.

entries.name: TurtleBot 4
entries.def: The standard issue teaching robot of the ROS curriculum.

entries.name: TurtleBot3
entries.def: Small open source research and teaching robot with a spinning laser scanner, used in university courses and labs to learn mapping and navigation.
specs: Two servo driven wheels with a caster
360 degree laser distance sensor, inertial unit and wheel encoders, with a camera on the Waffle Pi
Runs open source mapping and navigation software on a single board computer
facts: Burger and Waffle Pi models share the same software stack
Developed with Open Robotics as a reference learning platform
Waffle Pi carries up to 30 kg and reaches 0.26 m per second

entries.name: Tux Droid
entries.def: Cordless penguin robot styled after Tux, the mascot of Linux, that was manufactured by the company KYSOH and came out around 2007.

entries.name: Twendy-One
entries.def: A wheeled care humanoid with soft hands able to hold an egg or support a person standing.

entries.name: TyBot
entries.def: Self propelled gantry robot that rolls along a bridge deck rebar mat and ties intersections automatically without needing a building information model.
specs: Self propelled wheeled gantry spanning the deck with a robotic rebar tying head
Machine vision that locates rebar intersections without a pre loaded digital model
Autonomously locates and ties intersections across the mat with one operator supervising
facts: Used on highway bridge deck projects across the United States
Removes a repetitive stooped labour task associated with worker injury
The same company builds IronBot, which lifts and places reinforcing bar

entries.name: Ultra
entries.def: General purpose robot for repetitive industrial tasks such as packing, installed in hours without custom integration.

entries.name: Ultra Trencher 1
entries.def: Submersible trenching robot that buries undersea pipelines by cutting trenches in the seabed, described as the largest submersible robot in the world.
facts: Mass of 60 tons; 7.8 m long, 7.8 m wide and 5.6 m tall
Trenches pipelines up to 1 m in diameter at depths of up to 1,500 m
Cuts trenches with a pair of jet swords that force pressurised water into sediment

entries.name: Ulysses
entries.def: Bomb detecting robot used at Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos in Greece, the country's largest international airport.

entries.name: Unimate
entries.def: Industrial robot regarded as the first of its kind, which went to work on a General Motors assembly line in New Jersey in 1961.
facts: Worked at the Inland Fisher Guide Plant in Ewing Township, New Jersey
Produced as a family of related robots

entries.name: Uniroo
entries.def: One legged robot built in the United States in 1991 and now exhibited at the MIT Museum.

entries.name: Unitree A1
entries.def: Twelve kilogram electric quadruped that brought dynamic legged research hardware down to a price universities could buy in quantity.
specs: In house brushless motors with planetary gear reduction
Inertial measurement unit, foot contact sensors, optional depth camera
Onboard balance control with a low level developer interface
facts: Widely used as a low cost research platform for learned locomotion controllers
Priced at a small fraction of comparable Western research quadrupeds

entries.name: Unitree B2
entries.def: Sixty kilogram industrial quadruped from Unitree rated to walk with forty kilograms of payload for more than four hours.
specs: High torque in house brushless joint motors, three per leg
Onboard perception and navigation with a developer interface
facts: Rated for standing loads of 120 kg and walking loads above 40 kg
IP67 sealed for outdoor industrial and emergency response use

entries.name: Unitree G1
entries.def: Compact humanoid priced from around 13,500 dollars, sold in volume to developers, universities and companies as an affordable locomotion and manipulation platform.
specs: In house electric joint modules with dual encoders and 90 newton metre knee torque
9,000 milliamp hour lithium battery giving roughly two hours
3D lidar, depth camera, four microphone array
Unitree software development kit with reinforcement learning training environments
facts: Listed from about 13,500 dollars, undercutting most full size humanoids
EDU configuration extends the robot to as many as 43 degrees of freedom
Performed a mass choreographed routine on Chinese state television in 2025

entries.name: Unitree Go1
entries.def: Consumer priced electric quadruped that Unitree marketed as a walking companion, starting at around two thousand seven hundred dollars.
specs: In house brushless motors with planetary gear reduction
Multiple stereo camera pairs, ultrasonic sensors, foot force sensors
Person following and obstacle avoidance, low level control on developer versions
facts: Launched from about 2,700 US dollars, undercutting every comparable quadruped at the time
Its side following mode was built to keep pace with a person on foot

entries.name: Unitree Go2
entries.def: Fifteen kilogram consumer and developer quadruped with a hemispherical lidar, sold from well under two thousand US dollars.
specs: In house brushless joint motors, three per leg
Hemispherical lidar with full 360 degree horizontal coverage, wide angle camera, foot force sensors on education models
Onboard obstacle avoidance and person following, developer interface on education versions
facts: Launched in 2023 from about 1,600 US dollars, among the cheapest dynamic quadrupeds sold
Offered in consumer, professional and education variants of the same platform

entries.name: Unitree H1
entries.def: Full size electric biped sold at a fraction of Western prices, notable for a fast recorded walking speed and for widespread laboratory adoption.
specs: In house electric joint modules with knee torque near 360 newton metres
3D lidar and depth camera giving 360-degree perception
Software development kit with reinforcement learning training environments
facts: Recorded moving at 3.3 metres per second, among the fastest for a full size humanoid
Sold into research and demonstration work at a small fraction of Western humanoid prices
Widely used as a base platform for third party arms, hands and compute

entries.name: Unitree H2
entries.def: Unitree's flagship full size humanoid with more human proportions and 31 joints, aimed at performance, service and research customers.
specs: Electric joint modules rated to 360 newton metres in the legs and 120 in the arms
Depth camera and lidar with microphone array
Unitree control stack with reinforcement learning training environments
facts: Unveiled in October 2025 with a more human silhouette than earlier Unitree humanoids
Thirty one joints including a three axis waist and two axis neck
Demonstrated dance and martial arts routines at launch

entries.name: Unitree R1
entries.def: Humanoid robot introduced by the Chinese company Unitree Robotics in 2025, standing 123 cm tall.

entries.name: UR10e
entries.def: Long reach e-Series arm from Universal Robots used for palletising, packaging and machine tending.

entries.name: UR16e
entries.def: Heavy payload member of the Universal Robots e-Series, built for loading machines and carrying heavy tools.

entries.name: UR20
entries.def: Redesigned collaborative arm from Universal Robots with new joints, aimed at palletising and welding.

entries.name: UR30
entries.def: Compact high payload arm from Universal Robots that shares the joint design of the UR20.

entries.name: UR3e
entries.def: Smallest arm of the Universal Robots e-Series, sized for benchtop assembly and screwdriving.

entries.name: UR5
entries.def: Six axis arm from Universal Robots that was among the first robots sold to work beside people without a safety cage.
facts: Payload of 5 kg and reach of 850 mm
Succeeded by the UR5e in 2018

entries.name: UR5e
entries.def: Medium sized e-Series arm from Universal Robots with a built in force and torque sensor at the tool flange.

entries.name: USV Maxlimer
entries.def: Uncrewed surface vessel run by the British firm SEA-KIT International that can work semi autonomously or under remote control, and won the Shell Ocean Discovery X Prize.
facts: Afterwards served to demonstrate uncrewed offshore operations beyond the horizon

entries.name: USV RSV
entries.def: Unmanned surface vessel developed since 2008 by the founders of the company Marine Tech SAS.

entries.name: UVD Robot
entries.def: Mobile ultraviolet disinfection robot that drives itself around hospital rooms and exposes surfaces to short wavelength light after manual cleaning.
specs: Differential drive base carrying a vertical array of ultraviolet C lamps
Lidar, three 3D cameras and passive infrared motion sensors
Map based route recording with autonomous, semi manual and static modes
facts: Developed with Odense University Hospital in Denmark
Shipped in large numbers during the 2020 pandemic response
A third generation Model C followed in 2020

entries.name: UWA Telerobot
entries.def: Remotely operated robot dating from 1996, run by the University of Western Australia's School of Mechanical and Civil Engineering.
facts: Belongs to the School of Mechanical and Civil Engineering at UWA

entries.name: Vaimos
entries.maker: IFREMER and École nationale supérieure de techniques avancées Bretagne
entries.def: French autonomous sailing boat carrying onboard instruments for measuring the ocean surface, developed by IFREMER and ENSTA Bretagne.

entries.name: Valkyrie
entries.def: NASA's first walking humanoid, built in about fifteen months for the 2013 DARPA Robotics Challenge and later loaned to university laboratories.
specs: Series elastic rotary and linear actuators
Rotating lidar and stereo head, torso hazard cameras, pelvis inertial units
facts: Designed and built in about fifteen months for the 2013 DARPA Robotics Challenge
Units loaned to MIT, Edinburgh, Northeastern and UT Austin

refs.label: Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center website

entries.name: Vanderbilt exoskeleton
entries.def: Powered exoskeleton from Vanderbilt University's Center for Intelligent Mechatronics, sold as Indego, meant to help people affected by paraplegia, stroke or other forms of paralysis walk on their own.
facts: Marketed under the name Indego
Parker Hannifin funded its further development
First commercial version was planned for release in 2015

entries.name: Vassar
entries.def: Gearless robot joints and arms driven by high torque transverse flux motors, built for AI research labs.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Vassar Robotics

entries.name: Vaucanson Flute Player
entries.def: Android automaton built by Jacques de Vaucanson that played a standard transverse flute of the period, imitating a human flautist; it was first exhibited in 1738.
facts: First shown publicly in 1738
Used an ordinary flute of the kind played by musicians of the day

entries.name: Vector
entries.def: A palm sized desk companion with big eyes and a cloud brain, revived by its fans.

entries.name: VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution
entries.def: Orthopedic surgical robot introduced by DePuy in 2021 to assist surgeons with total knee replacement operations.

entries.name: Versatran
entries.def: Cylindrical coordinate industrial robot from American Machine and Foundry, one of the earliest robots put to work in a factory.

entries.name: Versius
entries.def: Modular surgical robot from CMR Surgical whose arms sit on separate carts so they can be arranged around the operating table.

entries.name: VertiGo
entries.maker: ETH Zurich and Disney Research Zurich
entries.def: Remote controlled wall climbing robot on wheels, developed by ETH Zurich and Disney Research Zurich, that uses two fully tilting propellers to push itself onto and up walls.
facts: Its propellers can tilt through a full 360 degrees
Built on a carbon fiber baseplate with 3D printed joints
Can roll across the floor and then move onto a vertical wall

entries.name: VEX IQ
entries.def: Snap together plastic robotics kit used by schools and in the VEX IQ competitions.

entries.name: VideoRay ROVs
entries.def: Family of inspection class underwater remotely operated vehicles, each run from a control unit about the size of a suitcase and tethered by copper or fiber optic cable.
facts: Tether to the submersible can be copper or fiber optic

entries.name: VIPER
entries.def: Golf cart sized NASA rover built to hunt water ice at the lunar south pole with a metre long drill and neutron detector.
specs: Four independently steered and driven wheels able to work through soft regolith
Solar arrays with battery and headlights for shadowed driving
Navigation and hazard cameras, neutron spectrometer, near infrared volatiles spectrometer, mass spectrometer, one metre drill
Near real time driving by ground operators with onboard safety limits
facts: Built to drill for water ice in permanently shadowed craters
Cancelled in 2024 and revived in 2025 with a Blue Origin delivery
Planned surface mission of about 100 days

refs.label: Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center website

entries.name: Vitirover
entries.def: Small solar powered grazing robot that trims grass between vine rows and along railway verges, working inside a geofenced plot for days unattended.
specs: Four wheeled electric drive with a small rotary cutting blade
Onboard solar panel charging a battery, allowing continuous unattended work
Satellite positioning with geofence boundaries and remote telemetry
Grazes autonomously inside a geofenced plot for days, monitored remotely by a fleet handler
facts: Used under contract with the French railway operator SNCF to control vegetation on track verges
Deployed in Bordeaux vineyards as an alternative to herbicide and mechanical weeding
Designed to be light enough to work slopes and soft ground without compacting soil

entries.name: Vityaz-D
entries.def: Russian fully autonomous deep submergence vehicle built to reach full ocean depth, with a mass of 5650 kg.

entries.name: VolcanoBot 2
entries.def: Small two wheeled tethered robot built to crawl into volcanic fissures at Kilauea and map their inner shape in three dimensions.
specs: Two wheels with a tether for power, data and recovery
Camera and depth sensor for three dimensional mapping
facts: Descended 25 metres into a Kilauea fissure in 2014
Produced three dimensional maps of fissure interiors

entries.name: Vyommitra
entries.maker: Indian Space Research Organisation, Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre
entries.def: Half humanoid robot built by ISRO to fly on uncrewed Gaganyaan test missions and monitor cabin systems in place of a crew.
specs: Electric actuators in the head, torso and arms
Cameras and microphones for face and speech recognition, cabin parameter sensing
Monitors panels and answers crew questions in Hindi and English
facts: Built for uncrewed Gaganyaan test flights ahead of Indian crewed missions
Unveiled in January 2020 at a human spaceflight symposium in Bengaluru

refs.label: Indian Space Research Organisation, Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre website

entries.name: W3
entries.def: A hotel and building courier that rides lifts and passes through doors on its own.

entries.name: WABIAN-2R
entries.def: Full size biped used at Waseda to study human like walking, carrying a movable waist and trunk plus a passive toe joint.
specs: Direct current motors with harmonic drive gears and belt transmissions
Six axis force and torque sensors in the ankles, inertial sensing
facts: Walks with stretched knees using heel contact and toe off
Combines a two degree of freedom waist with a passive toe joint

refs.label: Waseda University, Humanoid Robotics Institute website

entries.name: WABOT-1
entries.def: Full scale anthropomorphic robot built at Waseda University that walked on two legs, gripped objects and held simple spoken exchanges.
specs: Hydraulic actuators in the lower limbs
Artificial vision system, tactile sensing in the hands, artificial ear
Separate onboard limb control, vision and conversation subsystems
facts: Widely cited as the first full scale anthropomorphic robot
Founded the Waseda line that led to WABOT-2 and WABIAN

entries.name: WABOT-2
entries.def: Keyboard playing humanoid from Waseda University that read printed sheet music with a camera eye and performed on an electronic organ.
specs: About 50 joints driven by electric motors
Camera eye for reading printed scores, microphone
facts: Read printed scores and played an electronic organ
Performed at Expo '85 in Tsukuba

entries.name: Wakamaru
entries.def: Yellow domestic robot from Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, built to interact with people in a natural way and offered only to Japanese households from 2005.
facts: Launched in 2005 at a price of $14,300 to $15,000
Also used at exhibitions, for guiding customers and as a receptionist
Never developed beyond its first model

entries.name: WALK-MAN
entries.def: Full size compliant humanoid built for European disaster response research and later tested in earthquake damaged buildings in Amatrice, Italy.
specs: Series elastic electric joints with 19 degree of freedom hands
Lidar, stereo cameras, joint torque and force sensing
Operator commanded with local autonomous functions
facts: Competed at the 2015 DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals
Field tested in earthquake damaged buildings in Amatrice

entries.name: Walker
entries.def: UBTech's first full size home humanoid, shown serving drinks at CES.

entries.name: Walker Chess player
entries.def: Purported chess playing automaton built in the 1820s by the Walker Brothers of Baltimore, Maryland, as a rival to the Turk, a widely known chess machine.
facts: Johann Nepomuk Mälzel, owner of the Turk, tried to buy it but was refused
Toured for several years before fading into obscurity

entries.name: Walker S
entries.def: An industrial humanoid piloted on automotive lines for quality inspection and assembly; deployed in fleets.

entries.name: Walker S2
entries.def: Industrial humanoid that swaps its own battery in about three minutes, sold to Chinese carmakers and electronics plants for continuous shift work.
specs: Electric joints with a high torque waist servo, plus autonomous battery exchange
Dual dynamically balanced battery packs with autonomous swap in about three minutes
Binocular stereo vision with RGB cameras
UBTECH fleet coordination software for multiple robots on a production line
facts: Swaps its own battery in about three minutes for continuous operation
Predecessor Walker S1 fleets deployed at Zeekr and Foxconn plants
UBTECH has reported some of the largest disclosed humanoid order books in China

entries.name: Walking Truck
entries.def: Hydraulic four legged vehicle from General Electric that an operator drove by moving his own arms and legs inside a force feedback harness.
specs: Hydraulic cylinders, three powered joints per leg
Onboard internal combustion engine driving hydraulic pumps
None, direct human force feedback teleoperation
facts: Built under the US Army Cybernetic Anthropomorphous Machine programme
Could lift loads of several hundred kilograms with a single leg
Preserved at the US Army Transportation Museum at Fort Eustis

entries.name: Wanda
entries.def: A wheeled home humanoid pitched at laundry and dishwashing.

entries.name: Warthog
entries.def: An amphibious heavyweight research vehicle for mines, farms and shorelines.

entries.name: Wave Glider
entries.def: Ocean surface robot whose submerged wing converts the motion of waves into forward thrust, with solar panels for its instruments.

entries.name: Whiz
entries.def: A vacuum sweeper trained by walking it once, then set loose on office carpets.

entries.name: WildCat
entries.def: Untethered petrol powered quadruped built to run fast in the open, the free running successor to the treadmill bound Cheetah.
specs: Hydraulic actuators with an articulated body
Onboard two stroke petrol engine driving a hydraulic pump
Onboard gait and balance control, remotely piloted
facts: Ran untethered at about 26 km/h, then the fastest recorded for a legged robot
Built under the DARPA Maximum Mobility and Manipulation programme

entries.name: Winbot
entries.def: Window cleaning robot from Ecovacs that holds itself to the glass by suction and wipes in a set pattern.

entries.name: WonderBorg
entries.def: Programmable six legged robot kit shaped like a beetle, released by Bandai in 2000 for use with the WonderSwan and Windows PCs.
facts: Released by Bandai in 2000
Has working antennae and six legs, imitating a beetle

entries.name: Workerbot
entries.def: Industrial robot from pi4 robotics GmbH whose movement and sensing abilities are modelled on those of a human.
facts: Name is a trademark of pi4 robotics GmbH

entries.name: WowWee Alive Chimpanzee
entries.def: Animatronic chimpanzee head from the WowWee Alive division of WowWee that uses motors and sensors to copy a live chimpanzee's facial expressions.
facts: First product in the WowWee Alive range
Eight motors drive its facial expressions
Nine sensors include infrared sensors in the eyes and touch sensors on the head

entries.name: XAG R150
entries.def: Compact wheeled farm vehicle that sprays orchards and carries loads along mapped routes, controlled from a phone and positioned by satellite reference stations.
specs: Four wheel drive electric chassis with interchangeable spray, spread and cargo modules
Corrected satellite positioning with reference station network, plus obstacle sensing
Autonomous route following from recorded or app drawn paths, with manual remote control available
facts: Sold alongside XAG's agricultural spraying drones as a ground counterpart
Used in orchards, tea gardens and vineyards where drone spraying is less suitable
Positioning relies on XAG's own network of satellite reference stations in China

entries.name: xArm 6
entries.def: Low cost six axis arm from UFactory popular with universities and small workshops.

entries.name: XGO-Mini
entries.def: A desktop quadruped with an arm on its back for pick and place tricks.

entries.name: Xianxingzhe
entries.def: First bipedal humanoid built in China, a 140 cm machine that walked at about two steps per second and was announced in November 2000.
facts: First bipedal humanoid robot built in China
Announced in November 2000 after development begun in the 1980s

refs.label: National University of Defense Technology website

entries.name: Xiaomanlv
entries.def: Low speed autonomous parcel van that delivers packages on Chinese university campuses and residential districts, developed by Alibaba and operated by its Cainiao logistics arm.
specs: Four wheeled low speed electric vehicle with a parcel locker body
Battery electric drive with swappable batteries
Level 4 autonomy limited to campuses and low speed roads, with remote monitoring
facts: Passed 10 million parcels delivered in 2022
Unveiled at Alibaba's Apsara conference in September 2020 as a DAMO Academy project
Deployed across several hundred university campuses in China

entries.name: XMAN-R1
entries.def: A wheeled embodied service humanoid from the restaurant robot leader.

entries.name: XR-2
entries.def: Educational robot manufactured by Rhino Robotics as a teaching tool for training students in robotics.

entries.name: XV-11
entries.def: The first consumer robot vacuum with a spinning laser scanner, which let it map a room and clean in straight overlapping rows.
specs: Two drive wheels with a wide fixed brush in a D shaped body
Rechargeable battery with a charging base
Spinning laser distance scanner with bumper and cliff sensors
Laser SLAM mapping with systematic row coverage and resume after charging
facts: First consumer robot vacuum to navigate with a laser scanner
Its inexpensive laser module was widely reused by robotics hobbyists
Neato Robotics shut down in 2023 after 18 years

entries.name: Yaoki
entries.def: Palm sized Japanese commercial rover with two wide wheels that can right itself, flown on the IM-2 mission but never deployed.
specs: Two wide wheels on a self righting body
facts: Named for a Japanese saying about rising after every fall
Undeployed after the IM-2 lander toppled in March 2025

entries.name: Yarbo
entries.def: A modular yard robot that swaps between snow blowing, mowing and leaf blowing bodies.

entries.name: Yeti
entries.def: Four wheeled polar survey robot that tows radar over Antarctic and Greenland ice to find crevasses and buried structures.
specs: Four wheel drive on a lightweight snow chassis
Ground penetrating radar with satellite navigation for survey grids
Autonomous waypoint following along programmed survey lines
facts: Surveys crevasse fields ahead of crewed polar traverses
Used to map buried structures at the South Pole station

entries.name: youBot
entries.def: Small omnidirectional base with a five axis arm, sold by KUKA to universities for research and teaching.

entries.name: YuMi
entries.def: Two armed collaborative robot from ABB, padded and lightweight, built for small parts assembly beside people.
facts: Model number IRB 14000
Name comes from the phrase you and me

entries.name: Yummy Future
entries.def: Robotic stations that take over repetitive preparation work in restaurants and food retail.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, Yummy Future

entries.name: Yutu
entries.def: China's first lunar rover, landed in Mare Imbrium by Chang'e 3, which lost mobility after one lunar day but kept transmitting for years.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive with four corner steering
Two folding solar panels with radioisotope heater units
Panoramic and hazard cameras, lunar penetrating radar, infrared imaging spectrometer, alpha particle X ray spectrometer
facts: First Chinese rover on the Moon
Its radar revealed at least nine distinct subsurface layers
Kept working more than 31 months despite failing after 114 metres

refs.label: China Academy of Space Technology website

entries.name: Yutu-2
entries.def: Chinese far side lunar rover delivered by Chang'e 4, the longest operating rover on the Moon, with 1,613 metres logged by September 2025.
specs: Six wheel rocker bogie drive with four corner steering
Folding solar panels with radioisotope heater units
Panoramic cameras, lunar penetrating radar, visible and near infrared imaging spectrometer, neutral atom detector
Teleoperated through a relay satellite with onboard hazard detection
facts: First rover to operate on the lunar far side
Passed Lunokhod 1 in November 2019 as the longest lived lunar rover
Radar profiles revealed layered ejecta deposits tens of metres thick

refs.label: China Academy of Space Technology website

entries.name: Zenbo
entries.def: A rolling home assistant that read bedtime stories in Taiwanese households.

entries.name: Zeta Surgical
entries.def: Image guidance and robotics platform that uses computer vision to register a patient in minutes for neurosurgical and transcranial magnetic stimulation procedures.

refs.label: Y Combinator company profile, ZETA SURGICAL

entries.name: ZEUS
entries.def: Surgical robot with arms controlled from a separate console, withdrawn after its maker merged with Intuitive Surgical in 2003.
facts: Used in 2001 for a transatlantic operation, with the surgeon in New York and the patient in Strasbourg

entries.name: ZEUS Robotic Surgical System
entries.def: Surgical robot made by Computer Motion that had three remotely controlled arms, won FDA clearance in 2001 and was dropped in 2003 after the merger with Intuitive Surgical.
facts: Cleared by the FDA in 2001
One arm, AESOP, was a voice controlled endoscope
Discontinued in 2003; Intuitive Surgical developed the da Vinci system instead

entries.name: Zhurong
entries.def: China's first Mars rover, which explored southern Utopia Planitia for a year and found evidence of water altered soils and buried shorelines.
specs: Six wheel active suspension able to crab sideways and lift wheels
Four foldable solar panels with a phase change heat storage system
Navigation and topography cameras, multispectral camera, ground penetrating radar, laser induced breakdown spectrometer, magnetometer, weather station
Ground planned drives with onboard hazard detection
facts: Made China the second nation to drive a rover on Mars
Travelled 1,921 metres before hibernating in May 2022
Radar data supported the case for ancient shoreline deposits

refs.label: China Academy of Space Technology website
China Academy of Space Technology website

entries.name: Zoë
entries.def: Solar powered astrobiology rover used in the Atacama Desert, the first robot to detect and map life autonomously in a desert.
specs: Four wheel drive with passive averaging suspension
Fluorescence imager, stereo cameras, spectrometers, one metre drill added later
Long autonomous traverses with onboard science target selection
facts: First robot to autonomously detect and map life in a desert
Returned to the Atacama with a one metre drill for subsurface samples

entries.name: Zoomer
entries.def: Interactive toy robot dog that responded to voice commands and learned tricks.
